Overview

What the letters mean: F Favourable hypothesis to be verifiedC Counter-evidence to be clarifiedP Missing premise

Which existing drugs, supplements, diets and other interventions are worth studying for the WWOX-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (WWOX-DEE)? This page shows what is observed in WWOX, what comes from other diseases or from predictions, what argues against, and which evidence is missing. A “need” is a biological aim: an observed alteration in a WWOX system on which an intervention could act.

To keep in mind. Research material for discussion with the treating clinical team: it is not medical advice nor an indication of treatment. A priority letter says why an intervention is worth studying, not how well it works: it is not a score nor a probability.

Main investigations to pursue

Order of the investigations to be funded: it assesses the value of the next discriminating test, not the efficacy of an intervention.

Provisional and reasoned order, with possible ties: each row is a question about a compound or intervention, its action, the context and the benefit sought, with a next test. It is not a ranking of treatments nor a probability of benefit; the depth of the evidence is indicated separately.

How the positions are decidedThe positions are judgements written by research agents and re-read row by row, not a predictive calculation. The code computes no position: it only checks that the fields are complete, that the vocabularies are closed, that the positions are consecutive, that the need and the unit cited exist, that no doses or claims of absolute absence appear and that a conditional hypothesis is never called qualified. Novelty gives no advantage: a new proposal rises only for the reasons written in its row. What is not known is not ineffective.
Three different things, kept separate in every row. Solidity of the evidence (how much is already measured, and where); priority of the next investigation (how much the next discriminating test is worth); development feasibility (how realistic it is to take the intervention beyond a research probe). One does not imply the others: a row may have weak evidence and high priority.

Compared with IT20. 10 unchanged, 0 moved, 0 new among the rows shown. The reason for each move is in the row.

  1. 1 (tie) AAV9-delivered human WWOX (gene addition) thread already known in WWOX thread with a result already in a card#
    Question
    Does neuronal WWOX restoration started AFTER symptom onset recover any endpoint, or only prevent one when given in the neonatal window?
    Reason for the priority
    Every partial-benefit lever in this module is ordered as a bridge to, or a substitute for, restoration; whether restoration works after onset decides which of those two framings is the real one, so one result re-reads the whole list.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    E4 - card reviewed, 12 WWOX-side assertion(s) read beyond abstract; class pharmacology table (IT7 P5)
    Decisive uncertainty
    No arm exists in which treatment begins after the phenotype is established; the window is stated, not measured against a later start, and P300 readouts are survivor-selected.
    Next test
    One added arm of the published design with injection after the first recorded spike-wave discharge, same endpoints, untreated same-genotype comparator kept. Worded per endpoint class: measure the restoration actually achieved at the age of treatment and its regional distribution, because the one comparable later-age failure in a short-lived null was left uninterpretable by that missing measurement; carry a within-animal pre-treatment recording, a treated wild-type or heterozygote arm, growth and glycaemia as primary endpoints (growth failed even with pre-onset treatment in the closest analogue), and follow-up long enough to see decay. Quantified myelin sheath structure (g-ratio or electron microscopy, not marker intensity) is the discriminating endpoint for a neuron-driven lesion: white-matter abnormality has been reversed after a documented onset only in glial or metabolic lesions, and sheath structure after onset has been reported only in a metabolic oligodendrocyte-enzyme lesion (G-ratio by electron microscopy, one source) and not in any neuron-driven lesion. Spike-wave rate is the confirmatory endpoint and its external precedent (not WWOX evidence) is split, so pair it with a rhythm or power-spectrum measure; interneuron number as well as excitability, because no source measured number.
    Scientific details of this row
    Origin of the proposal
    Named in the WWOX literature and carded: the neonatal AAV9 gene-addition study (cards C01 and C04).
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system, read beyond the abstract: the high-dose arm reaches a survival plateau to day 300 and lowers spike-wave discharges to a wild-type-indistinguishable level; weight is ordered against wild type and the untreated knockout (equal to the high dose at P30 only), and glycaemia is NOT shown to be prevented: at P10 the treated arms are not significantly different from the untreated knockout (high dose about 113, low dose about 105, untreated knockout about 95; Figure 3E, card C04 DR-AAV-GLU10-HD and DR-AAV-GLU10-LD), at P20 the untreated-knockout comparator is absent because those animals are dead (Figure 3F, DR-AAV-GLU20-LD and DR-AAV-GLU20-HD, direction UNKNOWN) and the P20 result is dose-graded against wild type only, and by P30 the dose separation has closed (Figure 3G); the paper's own text states that both doses partially corrected hypoglycaemia, while the panel does not support it (card C04 records this: the treated arms are not significantly different from the untreated knockout at P10); the glucose result depends on age, dose and comparison, and a non-significant difference at P10 is not evidence of no benefit. Every treated arm was injected in the stated neonatal window.
    Development feasibility
    Established model and established vector; the added arm is a timing change, not a new assay.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: the two gene-addition cards (C01, C04) and their assertion rows; the deepdive manifest of the source; the work-order statements for this need. Checked for a post-onset arm and found none. Not a statement about the literature beyond the sources this module has read. Extended on 2026-11-05/06 by two bounded external searches (batch_sci_20261105, r1 and r2 query logs, 66 queries in all): conditional, antisense and vector restoration after onset in Mecp2, Ube3a, Fmr1, Tsc1, Pten, Syngap1, Cdkl5, Shank3, Tcf4, Scn1a, Scn1b, Kcnt1, Scn8a and leukodystrophy models. The earlier of the two searches was anchored on gene names and could not reach enzyme, connexin, tubulin or astrocyte-transporter leukodystrophies; an independent review found post-onset white-matter arms there. Bounded searches, not a statement that none exists.
    Reason for the move
    position unchanged from IT20 (rank 1): No IT21 input changes the position. The row text was corrected in IT21 P1 (glycaemia is not called prevented).
  2. 1 (tie) Integrated-stress-response modulators (class) new hypothesis generated by LEGEND measurement of a premise, without a compound#
    Question
    Before any ISR-attenuating compound can be ordered: in a WWOX-deficient HUMAN neural system, does the ISR run high or low?
    Reason for the priority
    The need's direction is unresolved and the two available readouts disagree by design, so no compound on this axis can be qualified either way. Resolving the sign is the cheapest act that converts the largest blocked slice of the catalogue into an orderable or a refused question; leaving it unresolved keeps that slice invisible rather than negative.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    E3 - card reviewed with assertions; no WWOX-side result read beyond abstract
    Decisive uncertainty
    Which sign the ISR actually has at protein level in a WWOX-deficient human neural cell, and in which cell type. The IT28 reading of the transferable literature adds that the sign of a lever depends on which node is perturbed and on the stress class (chronic misfolded cargo versus a locked eIF2B lesion versus transient external stress), and that RNA target sets can disagree with eIF2-alpha phosphorylation in both directions. Until the protein-level sign is measured, an ISR-attenuating and an ISR-potentiating compound remain equally defensible.
    Next test
    ATF4 protein, total and phosphorylated eIF2-alpha and per-cell translation (nascent-protein labelling) in a WWOX-deficient human neural line against an isogenic control, at one differentiation stage and by cell type, no compound involved. Only if the sign is high, a pre-registered panel: an eIF2B activator and kinase-level loss against genetic PPP1R15A loss, with a second-stressor arm and a functional endpoint. IT30 (design hypothesis only, from the residues of CH-IT28-ISR-ROLE read in wo06_it30_20261106 and independently checked): keep a network-activity or seizure-relevant readout beside the protein-level sign; if a potentiation arm is tried, make it genetic (a PPP1R15B knockdown) or chemical with measured p-eIF2alpha and an alpha-2 control (guanabenz acts on alpha-2 receptors and Sephin1 and guanabenz were not shown to inhibit PPP1R15A-PP1); the only mammalian seizure-endpoint precedent for a potentiator is two studies of one eIF2-alpha phosphatase inhibitor with opposite signs, so no arm is promoted.
    Scientific details of this row
    Origin of the proposal
    Generated by LEGEND from the qualified need path: the direction of the integrated stress response is unresolved (IT20).
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system transcript-level only and contradictory: the knockout organoid shows the ISR target set lower, one shRNA library per arm shows it higher, and the designs are not comparable. No ATF4 protein and no eIF2-alpha phosphorylation measurement exists in the sources read.
    Development feasibility
    A protein measurement on material the module already reasons about; no new model and no compound needed.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: this need's eleven observation rows and their readout levels; the ISR card and its assertions; the search layer over the eight ISR targets (78 associations, 56 families, none direction-coherent because the need direction is unresolved). The gap is a missing measurement in the sources this module has read, not a claim about the ISR literature.
    Reason for the move
    position unchanged from IT20 (rank 1): IT28 challenge CH-IT28-ISR-ROLE (batches on the neuronal and the glial/myelin literature) changes what the test must measure and which result would discriminate, not the position.
  3. 2 (tie) T-type calcium blockade, proposed isoform-reach set to verify (efonidipine, flunarizine, against the carded T-type agents) new hypothesis generated by LEGEND thread with a result already in a card#
    Question
    Which T-type isoform carries the suppression of the provoked seizure phase, and does the effect depend on the genotype?
    Reason for the priority
    The module's one T-type result is complex-or-group level with no isoform datum and no drug-by-genotype interaction test, and its own need file names both gaps. Two approved compounds are proposed as a pair that MAY differ in isoform reach; the pair is a proposal to verify, not a documented discriminating pair: the catalogue difference between them (one T-type target row for the first agent, three for the second) comes from annotation completeness, not from a documented functional selectivity, because in the catalogue both are tagged selectivity Not Determined and no fitted potency on the three isoforms is carried for the first agent (ChEMBL holds no calcium-channel activity for it), while the second has Kd values on all three only from synthesis papers that used it as a reference, in different assays and conditions. Absence of a subtype in a catalogue is not inactivity. Both agents also act on other targets (L-type channels for one, receptors beyond the channel family for the other), so the potency measures in one assay and species, at the concentration reached in the animal, are the first step.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    E3 - card reviewed with assertions; no WWOX-side result read beyond abstract
    Decisive uncertainty
    Whether the carded effect is a T-type effect at all, which isoform carries it, and whether it is genotype-dependent. Whether the two agents really differ in isoform reach at the concentrations used is itself unmeasured. The same effect from two compounds is compatible with a common target (the T-type class) and does not by itself weaken the T-type attribution; it only fails to discriminate isoforms. What would weaken the attribution is no effect of either agent at on-target exposure, an effect that tracks off-target activity rather than T-type potency, or an equal effect in wild type (no genotype dependence).
    Next test
    The published provoked-seizure design with a drug-by-genotype interaction term and the proposed pair beside the carded agent, after the potency of each agent on the three isoforms has been qualified in one assay and species; identical provocation and scoring.
    Scientific details of this row
    Origin of the proposal
    Reached from the T-type calcium need through the catalogue path; the proposed pair is a proposal to verify (IT20).
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system: a T-type blocker suppressed the late phase of the provoked seizure score in the null mouse, one experiment, genotype specificity not established by an interaction. Catalogue: direction-coherent blocker actions on CACNA1G, CACNA1H and CACNA1I, at group and single-protein level, from curated mechanism rows.
    Development feasibility
    Published assay, approved compounds, three arms added to an existing design.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: the search layer over CACNA1G, CACNA1H and CACNA1I (190 associations, 66 families); the T-type card and the ethosuximide and apinocaltamide units; the uncarded-items table; the IT9 to IT11 qualification records; a name scan of every card and ranking table for each proposed compound. Both proposals are absent from that WWOX material and are members of a class the module already holds, so this is a proposed probe set to verify, not a new biological relation.
    Reason for the move
    position unchanged from IT20 (rank 2): No IT21 input changes the position. The row text was corrected in IT21 P1 (the pair is a proposal to verify, not a documented discriminating pair). IT29: in other models the sign of several channel-agent classes flips with the lesion class; a discriminating challenge in the WWOX slice preparation would separate an inhibition-loss-like from an excitatory-gain-like network.
  4. 2 (tie) Ethosuximide (and the carded T-type thread) thread already known in WWOX thread with a result already in a card#
    Question
    Is the carded suppression specific to WWOX loss, or does the same agent act equally in wild type?
    Reason for the priority
    The position of this thread rests on a single laboratory and a single paper in which the comparison drug acted better, and the specificity flag is an unknown rather than a clean reading. The thread is already ordered, so the result changes a standing position rather than adding a new one.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    E4 - card reviewed, 1 WWOX-side assertion(s) read beyond abstract
    Decisive uncertainty
    Whether an interaction term survives; a wild-type effect of the same size would move this thread out of its group without any new compound being involved.
    Next test
    The same provoked-seizure design with both genotypes treated and an interaction term, powered on the published effect size.
    Scientific details of this row
    Origin of the proposal
    Carded thread: the T-type suppression of the provoked seizure phase in the null mouse.
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system with a specificity flag: one paper, one laboratory, no drug-by-genotype test, and a wild-type arm whose variability is comparable to the effect.
    Development feasibility
    The assay exists and the compound is carded; this is the control arm the original design omitted.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: the ethosuximide and apinocaltamide units, their assertion rows and caveat rows, and the per-need position table. The missing interaction test is recorded in this module's own caveats, not inferred from absence.
    Reason for the move
    position unchanged from IT20 (rank 2): No IT21 input changes the position. IT29: epilepsy-model screens in other genotypes give no corroboration for this agent (absence of corroboration is not refutation); the position rests on the single pup experiment.
  5. 3 (tie) NMDAR antagonism (the carded tool compound and the clinically used class) thread already known in WWOX thread with a result already in a card#
    Question
    Does a clinically used NMDAR antagonist reproduce the burst suppression obtained with the tool compound, at a stated extracellular magnesium concentration?
    Reason for the priority
    This is the only axis in the module with a measured WWOX-system drug readout, and it was obtained with a full competitive block by a tool compound. Whether a partial block reproduces it is the step between a perturbation result and an orderable question; the magnesium dependence makes the result uninterpretable unless the bath is reported.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    E4 - card reviewed, 1 WWOX-side assertion(s) read beyond abstract; class pharmacology table (IT7 P5)
    Decisive uncertainty
    Whether a partial, clinically achievable block suffices, and whether the carded effect is a subunit effect or a pore-block effect. A pore blocker's potency depends on voltage and on magnesium, so the unreported bath is itself the obstacle.
    Next test
    Repeat the slice burst assay with the magnesium concentration reported, a partial-block agent beside the tool compound, and the untreated same-genotype comparator.
    Scientific details of this row
    Origin of the proposal
    Carded axis: burst suppression by NMDAR block in the slice.
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system: blocking NMDAR abolished the burst in the WWOX-deficient slice, one drug, one preparation. The recording bath magnesium is not stated in the source, and the incubation solution already contains magnesium.
    Development feasibility
    The slice preparation exists; the change is a reported bath and one added arm.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: this need's eight observation rows, the two NMDAR cards and their assertions, and the search layer over the eight receptor-subunit targets (709 associations, 187 families). The module's own need file records that the clinically used agents were not found to have been given to a WWOX system in the sources read.
    Reason for the move
    position unchanged from IT20 (rank 3): No IT21 input changes the position.
  6. 3 (tie) Pro-myelinating agents (class) new hypothesis generated by LEGEND measurement of a premise, without a compound#
    Question
    Is there an axonal signal left for a pro-myelinating agent to act on, before any such agent is ordered?
    Reason for the priority
    This need carries 318 catalogue associations and not one of them is direction-coherent: a restore-type need has no action vocabulary in the catalogue to match, so the slice looks empty for a structural reason, not a biological one. The premise question is cheaper than any compound test and decides whether the axis is a target or a consequence.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    E2 - card reviewed, abstention (premise named, no test designed)
    Decisive uncertainty
    Whether the neuron still emits the activity-dependent signal that a pro-myelinating agent would amplify. If it does not, the whole class is not a lever here regardless of its pharmacology. IT29: even where an intrinsic route works, whether it acts when the lesion is neuronal is untested.
    Next test
    Measure the axonal activity-dependent myelination signal in the WWOX-deficient system against an isogenic control, before any compound; then decide whether the class is orderable. IT29: add an arm in Wwox-null precursor monoculture or the Wwox-null neuron co-culture, with a lipid-synthesis comparator beside the muscarinic one, crossed with a neuronal-activity manipulation.
    Scientific details of this row
    Origin of the proposal
    Generated by LEGEND from the myelination need (IT20).
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system: the myelin deficit is partly prevented when WWOX is restored in neurons in the neonatal window; the treated arms of the source are unquantified, and whether an established deficit re-myelinates is unmeasured. IT29: perturbation evidence from other systems signs several intrinsic precursor-differentiation routes (muscarinic-receptor, lipid-synthesis, thyroid- and RXR-type receptor) in wild-type or injury settings and none in a neuron-driven hypomyelination model; HDAC3 loss is adverse for maturation; an independent screen disagrees with some signs.
    Development feasibility
    A measurement in an existing system; no compound and no new model.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: this need's three observation rows; the pro-myelinating class unit and its abstention; the search layer over the six myelination targets (546 associations, 313 families, none direction-coherent). The emptiness is a vocabulary mismatch this package measured, not a claim that no pro-myelinating literature exists.
    Reason for the move
    position unchanged from IT20 (rank 3): No IT21 input changes the position. The thyroid-hormone probe row asks the receptor-responsiveness question on the same axis; the two are not merged because one measures the neuron's signal and the other the precursor cell's response. IT29 (phenotype-first table): position unchanged; the added evidence is transferred from non-WWOX systems and conditional.
  7. 4 (tie) Dichloroacetate and PDK inhibition thread already known in WWOX measurement of a premise, without a compound#
    Question
    Is there a PDH block in a WWOX-deficient human neural cell at all, and does its direction match the one this lever assumes?
    Reason for the priority
    The chain that motivates this lever predicts a PDH block, and the two available data point the other way: the kinase transcript is down and the one human activity measurement shows no difference. Ordering the compound before the premise is measured is how a plausible chain becomes a wasted experiment.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    E3 - card reviewed with assertions; no WWOX-side result read beyond abstract; class pharmacology table (IT7 P5)
    Decisive uncertainty
    Whether PDH flux is actually reduced. The lever's direction is derived from the chain, not from a measurement, and the available signs contradict it.
    Next test
    PDH activity and flux in a WWOX-deficient human neural cell against an isogenic control, with the glycolytic readout measured in the same material.
    Scientific details of this row
    Origin of the proposal
    Carded chain: dichloroacetate and PDK inhibition on the pyruvate axis.
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system: a glycolytic signature; the kinase transcript lower in the organoid; no difference in the one human PDH activity measurement. The kinase-to-PDH link has no WWOX observation.
    Development feasibility
    An established assay on material the module already uses.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: this need's ten observation rows and their readout levels; the dichloroacetate and HIF-axis units; the search layer over the eight axis targets (209 associations, 180 families, none direction-coherent because the need direction is unresolved).
    Reason for the move
    position unchanged from IT20 (rank 4): No IT21 input changes the position. One IT21 rejection (an inhibitor of class I histone deacetylases proposed to lower SLC2A1) touches the same glycolysis theme and is listed under what the generator rules out.
  8. 4 (tie) The NRF2 (KEAP1) axis, genetic arm before any compound thread already known in WWOX measurement of a premise, without a compound#
    Question
    Does lowering KEAP1 or raising NRF2 change a functional readout in a WWOX-deficient neural cell, in the direction the two conditional arms of this need assume?
    Reason for the priority
    Both arms of this need are explicitly conditional and neither is established, and the module has already refused to read agreement between two electrophiles as evidence of pathway dependence. A genetic arm answers the dependence question that no compound pair can answer.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    E3 - card reviewed with assertions; no WWOX-side result read beyond abstract
    Decisive uncertainty
    Whether the axis is engaged at all in a WWOX-deficient neural cell, and whether engaging it helps or harms. No compound in the record acts in such a cell. IT22: the AhR-target transcript is higher in the knockout while NFE2L2 is lower, so engagement of the axis is not even directionally clear.
    Next test
    Genetic KEAP1 lowering with a functional readout in the WWOX-deficient neural system, isogenic control, before any electrophile is compared.
    Scientific details of this row
    Origin of the proposal
    Carded axis: the NRF2/KEAP1 need with two conditional arms.
    Available evidence
    Outside WWOX for the pharmacology; WWOX-system only for the raised reactive-oxygen readouts, whose sign differs by context between a fly and late-passage fibroblasts and does not reconcile. IT22: the organoid NFE2L2 transcript (0.75x) is now a generator input (new question, role unknown, second system failed its control); the generator returns a topical AhR-pathway agent and agents that block EZH2 as conditional rows, and the canonical NRF2 activators only as diagnostic direct hits on the seed gene itself.
    Development feasibility
    Standard genetic perturbation; the readout is the constraint, not the reagent.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: this need's three observation rows; the NRF2-axis unit and the IT10 and IT11 qualification records on it; the search layer over NFE2L2 and KEAP1 (890 associations, 863 families, none direction-coherent because the need direction is unresolved).
    Reason for the move
    position unchanged from IT20 (rank 4): No IT21 input changes the position. An ALOX15 proposal on the same axis was left inconclusive in IT21 (no neural WWOX measurement). IT22: unchanged position; a new generator input reaches the axis but adds no measurement.
  9. 5 (tie) Lithium thread already known in WWOX thread with a result already in a card#
    Question
    Should this thread stay in the selection, given that its only pharmacology acts against a second need of the same objective?
    Reason for the priority
    The thread is carried by one paper from one laboratory, the agent is non-selective, and it pushes the canonical Wnt readout in the direction this module's other need wants lowered. The question now is whether to keep it, not what to measure next with it: that is a decision a single interaction test can settle.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    E4 - card reviewed, 1 WWOX-side assertion(s) read beyond abstract
    Decisive uncertainty
    Whether any part of the carded effect is attributable to the named kinase rather than to the agent's other actions, and whether the opposing push on the second need is tolerable.
    Next test
    A selective inhibitor of the named kinase beside the non-selective agent in the same WWOX-system assay, with the second need's readout measured in the same experiment. IT21 addition: include an arm with the inositol precursor added back, which tests the second action in the same experiment.
    Scientific details of this row
    Origin of the proposal
    Carded thread: lithium.
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system with a specificity flag: one paper, one laboratory, the comparison drug reported better; the kinase output readout is a phosphorylation site in mouse plus a docking mechanism in cells. IT21 addition (P3b, proposal G02): the same provocation test in the null, heterozygous and wild-type littermates shows the lithium effect in all three genotypes, and a second documented action of lithium (inositol monophosphatase inhibition) has a documented pro-convulsant sign in rodents, which disfavours it as the mediator by analogy (the precedent is the lithium-pilocarpine model, not a measurement in the Wwox assay; Cheng 2020 also ran a pilocarpine model in Wwox mice, so the objection that the provocations differ is testable in the same system); abstract-level reading for the sign argument.
    Development feasibility
    Selective tool compounds exist; the assay is the carded one.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: this need's two observation rows; the lithium unit, its caveat rows and its counter-statements; the search layer over the four kinase-axis targets (588 associations, 526 families, none direction-coherent because the need direction is unresolved). The opposing action on the second need is recorded in this module's own need file.
    Reason for the move
    position unchanged from IT20 (rank 5): Position unchanged from IT20. The ten-row ceiling does not displace a row that carries a risk flag or human clinical reports in favour of a conditional probe (the rule stated in the curation block of the context), so this row stays at rank 5 and the two new IT21 conditional probes sit at rank 6, below the line. New IT21 input: the inositol-monophosphatase route to the lithium effect is DISFAVOURED_BY_SIGN_PRECEDENT (an analogy from the lithium-pilocarpine model, not a measurement in the Wwox assay; see what the generator rules out). That result is not what supports this row's concern that the effect is not specific to WWOX loss: the concern comes from the +/+ arm of Cheng 2020 Figure 7d, where lithium suppresses the seizure stage as in the null. Cheng 2020 also ran a pilocarpine model in Wwox mice, so the objection that the two provocations differ is testable in the same system; the inositol arm of that proposal is folded into this row's next test.
  10. 5 (tie) GABA-aminotransferase inactivators (the carded clinical thread) thread already known in WWOX thread with a result already in a card#
    Question
    What does the published symptomatic response predict, and what does it not predict, about developmental outcome?
    Reason for the priority
    This is the thread with real human reports behind it and the one most likely to be read as a recommendation. The module already holds a series in which symptomatic response and developmental outcome did not move together, so the useful investigation is the separation itself, not another symptomatic observation.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    E3 - card reviewed with assertions; no WWOX-side result read beyond abstract
    Decisive uncertainty
    Whether the separation of symptomatic response and development seen in WWOX-DEE cases differs from the base rate of genetic and structural DEEs, in which a responder with poor development is the expected case (in unknown aetiology the two are coupled, so the base rate does not extend to DEE generally); whether any WWOX-DEE case shows a change on a continuous developmental measure after a symptomatic response; whether a sustained response, which no published child achieved, is followed by gain; and whether the separation holds for residual-function alleles. The earlier contradiction with the mechanism argument is not unexplained: other genetic DEE cohorts (STXBP1, Dravet, KCNQ2; partial full-text and abstract depth, not WWOX evidence) report a developmental component independent of seizure control.
    Next test
    EXECUTED 2026-11-05: the published same-genotype cases with both a symptomatic and a developmental endpoint were assembled (6 children with both endpoints; a discordance rate is not computable at n below 10, so counts are given instead). Vigabatrin fired the 5-or-more branch (counts with sources); hormonal therapy, diet and cannabidiol fired the fewer-than-5 branch (not computable from the public record). Next: read these counts against the stratum base rates in a2_baseline/README.md section 1.3; only a WWOX-DEE responder rate with a favourable or improving developmental course clearly above the genetic-DEE base rate would be a WWOX finding. Denominator request, without contact: for each WWOX-DEE series that reports an intervention, the number exposed, the response definition, and a dated developmental instrument before and after a sustained response; where a source gives one, compare within-child continuous scores, since a cut at 70 cannot discriminate. The five-patient series and Choi 2026 come first, and the seven-child series (PMID 42721537) is read when an open route exists. No new exposure is proposed.
    Scientific details of this row
    Origin of the proposal
    Carded clinical thread: GABA-transaminase inactivators.
    Available evidence
    Clinical reports only. Children counted once across 14 reports: 36 to 38 exposed to at least one of vigabatrin, hormonal therapy, ketogenic diet or cannabidiol (partial full-text depth in 11 reports, one source at abstract level). Both a symptomatic and a developmental outcome are recorded for 6. In 4 of them, a partial or transient improvement came with development unchanged; in 2, neither moved. No sustained, instrumented response is recorded, and no developmental gain follows any of the four classes. Vigabatrin: 5 children with both endpoints in 4 reports (4 discordant, 1 concordant non-response); these are not independent of the other classes, since three of the five also supply them and all five were on co-therapy. Children with both endpoints, by class, of those exposed: hormonal 3 of 11; ketogenic diet 2 of 12; cannabidiol 1 of 7. Counts only, no percentage (n below 10). Developmental statements are clinical narratives without a scale. A brain-imaging safety signal is recorded beside them in two children (abstract level, a report selected for the finding), so it is not a frequency. No WWOX child is recorded with a developmental gain after a symptomatic improvement. Four children in three reports (two of them in one report) had a partial, transient or clinically-defined improvement with development not progressing; two had neither. That is what the baseline in other genetic and structural early-onset encephalopathies predicts (a responder with poor development is the majority outcome in infantile spasms and near-universal in genetic strata), so it is not by itself a WWOX-specific feature. The comparison holds only as a binary: the baseline uses standardised scores with a cut, every WWOX developmental statement is a clinician narrative, and no WWOX child had a sustained, instrumented response. Non-WWOX DEE baseline (batch_sci_20261105 a2_baseline; not WWOX evidence): in a prospective IESS cohort read at partial full-text depth, 72 percent of responders (126 of 175, computed from its Table 1) were below the developmental cut at 3 years, and no genetic-aetiology child reached a favourable outcome (0 of 49, a count over all genetic-aetiology children, not a responder rate). In two randomised IESS trials (abstract level), arms that raised early spasm cessation by 15 to 19 points showed no demonstrated developmental difference, with about one chance in four of detecting the difference that full mediation would predict. In TSC, two randomised trials of pre-onset prevention changed seizure endpoints without changing development to 36 months; they test prevention before onset, not response after onset. The person-level association (ICISS, abstract level: 15.9 VABS points higher with early cessation) is carried by unknown aetiology and a normal first neurological examination.
    Development feasibility
    A record-level analysis on material already in the module; no experiment.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: this need's three observation rows; the inactivator unit, its caveats and the safety flag; the chloride-gradient and inhibitory-hypofunction needs for the mechanism argument that contradicts the reports. Extended on 2026-11-05/06: the non-WWOX DEE baseline queried (UKISS, ICISS, the National Infantile Spasms Consortium records with no developmental outcome endpoint, lead-time cohorts, EPISTOP and PREVeNT, STXBP1, Dravet and KCNQ2 cohorts, and an early-infantile DEE cohort with burst suppression; a2_baseline/queries.tsv); 14 WWOX-DEE reports queried for exposure and both endpoints (a1_wwox_reports). Bounded queries, not a statement that nothing else exists.
    Reason for the move
    position unchanged from IT20 (rank 5): Position unchanged from IT20. The ten-row ceiling does not displace a row with real human clinical reports in favour of a conditional probe (curation rule), so this row stays at rank 5 and the two new IT21 conditional probes sit at rank 6, below the line. This row is a record-level analysis that needs no experiment budget and can proceed alongside.

Conditional hypotheses generated (not in the ranking) (4)

Conditional proposals shown beside the ordered list, not within it: the ten-row limit keeps them out of the numbering, and no position is implied either by the order in which they appear or by their absence from the list. Each row is a research question with a probe, not a cure and not a qualified hypothesis: what is not known is not ineffective.

  • Agonist probe for the receptors of thyroid hormone (tiratricol, with liothyronine as comparator) external proposal transferred to the WWOX context conditional hypothesis, never presented as qualified
    Reference
    INV-12
    Question
    In a seizure-free neuron plus oligodendrocyte-precursor co-culture, does an agonist of the receptors for thyroid hormone release the maturation block seen after neuronal WWOX loss, and does it do so only in the WWOX-deficient condition?
    Origin of the proposal
    Carried in from another condition by a stated mechanistic analogy (a hormone-uptake defect with myelin and interneuron rescue) and reached through the compound-to-WWOX path (IT21 P3b, proposal G03, partial-benefit path; a related receptor arm, G10, was left inconclusive).
    Reason for the priority
    It is the role-resolving question the glia and myelin work left open (IT14): the maturation block is receptor-responsive or it is not, and one co-culture answers that before any in vivo question is asked. It enters at rank 6, below the ten-row line and behind the lithium and GABA-T rows (which carry a risk flag and human clinical reports and are not displaced by conditional probes), because the test is cell-level and inexpensive and an approved molecule exists for any later step, not because it is new: the precedent comes from a hormone-uptake defect in another disease and does not transfer by itself, and it sits below the two premise measurements (the dichloroacetate and NRF2 rows).
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system: precursor cells increased and mature oligodendrocytes decreased after neuron-restricted WWOX deletion, restored by neuronal add-back (IT14), with the add-back window early; the myelin deficit is partly prevented when WWOX is restored in neurons in the neonatal window. Outside WWOX: in a mouse model of a thyroid-hormone-uptake defect, a thyromimetic normalised myelination and interneuron differentiation only when started in the first three postnatal weeks (abstract-level reading). No myelin compound has been given to a WWOX system, and another myelin compound already has a negative developmental-myelination result in this module. IT22 P6 (partial full text of the two human trials of the molecule in a hormone-entry defect; mouse rescue; OPC literature at abstract level): the human precedent has no neurodevelopmental endpoint; the mouse rescue works only in postnatal weeks 1-3 and the effective dose suppressed the thyroid axis; precursor cells express receptor-alpha rather than receptor-beta in rodents (abstract level), so a receptor-beta-leaning liver-directed agent is an isoform control, not a candidate; seizure evidence is mixed (worsening in 3 patients with prior seizures; hyperthyroid rats more seizure-prone).
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    Conditional hypothesis: the WWOX-side pattern was read in IT14; the drug-side precedent was read at abstract level only; no WWOX-deficient measurement shows that the block responds to the receptor (no ranked unit, so no evaluation depth applies: this is not a depth of zero)
    Decisive uncertainty
    Whether the block is receptor-responsive and causal, or a consequence of seizures, or of the neuron's own signal being absent (the pro-myelinating-class row asks the premise from the signal side). The agent also has systemic actions that oppose the glycaemia need; an effect on seizure threshold was not looked up. IT22: the seizure-threshold question is now looked up and is mixed, not closed.
    Next test
    Seizure-free neuron plus precursor co-culture with wild-type and WWOX-deficient neurons: the agonist against vehicle and against hormone-depleted medium, with a receptor-isoform-selective control; read precursor and mature-cell counts. Correction in both genotypes means non-specific maturation; correction only in the deficient condition opens a pre-onset in vivo question; no change closes the route.
    Development feasibility
    Development feasibility: a cell-level probe is feasible now, and an approved thyroid-hormone molecule and a clinical-stage analogue exist; systemic hormone action, the early treatment window and the lack of a brain-exposure datum for the analogue limit any later use.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: a whole-word name search of this module and its registries on 2026-11-03 (no hit for either molecule) and the compound-to-WWOX path of IT21 P3b. A name search in this module, not a statement about the literature.
    ChEMBL register of the compound
    CHEMBL41632, CHEMBL1544 (ChEMBL identifiers (CC BY-SA 3.0, EMBL-EBI); the full register is in the separate ChEMBL file of the shareable package).
  • HSC70 (HSPA8) inhibitor peptide forigerimod, with lysosomal and genetic controls new hypothesis generated by LEGEND conditional hypothesis, never presented as qualified
    Reference
    INV-13
    Question
    Is a destabilised Q230P-class WWOX missense protein cleared by an HSC70-linked lysosomal step in neural cells, and when that step is blocked does the spared protein regain GSK3B-docking function?
    Origin of the proposal
    Generated by LEGEND: the compound-to-WWOX path found a curated inhibitor row on HSPA8 that the compound-to-need route had filed as not evaluable (IT21 P3b, proposal G01, broad-recovery path, track B).
    Reason for the priority
    It is the only broad-recovery path found in IT21, and it depends on the allele: the chase and knockdown test either closes the route or turns a detectable-protein result into a function question. It enters at rank 6 on that ground, below the ten-row line, behind the premise measurements and behind the two rows that carry a risk flag or human clinical reports, not on novelty; the compound is not a development candidate.
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system: the Q230P class shows no protein band with a normal transcript; a different missense (P252A) over-expressed in non-neural cells is cleared faster and restored by lysosomal inhibitors but not by a proteasome inhibitor. Compound side: a curated inhibitor action on HSPA8 exists; the one reference reports impaired HSC70 refolding and lower lysosomal degradation in lupus-mouse B cells (abstract-level reading). Nothing shows that the route and the allele are the same. IT22 P6: the peptide's measured binding is micromolar (7.32 uM by surface plasmon resonance), refolding is inhibited at 40 uM, and its own paper reads its action as flux slowing like a lysosomal-acidification inhibitor; the one measured rescue of a WWOX missense is over-expressed P252A in non-neural cells.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    Conditional hypothesis: the drug-side action is curated and its one reference was read at abstract level; no measurement in a WWOX-deficient neural cell connects the lysosomal step to the allele (no ranked unit, so no evaluation depth applies: this is not a depth of zero)
    Decisive uncertainty
    Whether the same step clears the Q230P-class protein in neural cells, and whether spared protein is functional (the degron and the GSK3B docking site may be one conformational event, giving a stable but inert protein). HSC70 also folds proteins, so blocking it may harm instead of help; the mirrored harm arm is carried as a second conditional arm. IT22: the weakest link is the substrate itself: no WWOX missense protein is shown above the assay floor, so gate 0 is a KO-controlled blot for the protein (the G372R line first).
    Next test
    Chase of the Q230P-class protein with HSPA8 and LAMP2 knockdown and a lysosomal-acidification inhibitor, then a docking-function read (phospho-tau, with the L404A docking mutant as control). No rise with knockdown closes the route; a rise without function closes deep recovery on this route; both rising earns a variant-specific preclinical question, still not qualified. IT22: one cycloheximide-chase design with HSPA8 and LAMP2A knockdown and a lysosomal-acidification inhibitor tests every stability lever; the peptide is one arm, not the lead.
    Development feasibility
    Development feasibility: low as a drug (a peptide whose one distribution study shows lungs and spleen, with no CNS exposure) and high as a cell-level probe. It depends on the allele and cannot serve a variant that makes no protein.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried: a whole-word name search of this module and its registries on 2026-11-03 (no hit for the peptide), the need file, and the catalogue, where a curated inhibitor row was filed as not evaluable by the compound-to-need route. A name search in this module, not a statement about the literature.

    Reference
    INV-14
    Question
    In Wwox-null versus wild-type mouse microglia and astrocyte cultures, does EZH2 inhibition lower or raise IL6 and TNF, with a second chemotype and Ezh2 knockdown as controls?
    Origin of the proposal
    Generated by LEGEND (generator refresh IT21 P2, proposal IT21P2-0195, harm arm of the cytokine question); a thread already generated in IT9 and re-emitted, qualified in IT21 P4a and kept conditional with the scope narrowed to mouse glial systems.
    Reason for the priority
    The chain was generated, not observed, and one reference cited by the chain itself reports the opposite sign, so the direction is not predicted. The test is feasible in existing mouse systems and one experiment can serve a second kinase-pathway probe. It sits at rank 7, below the ten-row line: the role of the inflammatory change (harm or protection) is unknown and the readout can wait for the glial measurements already planned.

    WWOX-system: the cytokine seeds are mouse transcript changes in two Wwox-deficient preparations; the human neural datasets carry no IL6 or TNF reads. Compound side: a selective, cell-active inhibitor of EZH2 with reported lowering of cytokines in a mouse brain model (abstract-level reading); a reference of the chain reports raised cytokines after EZH2 inhibition in glioma and microglia. IT22 P6 correction: the reference that carried the opposite sign used a different EZH2-blocking agent and siRNA, not the probe; in microglia the cytokines did not change and the rise came through medium from EZH2-suppressed tumour cells. Separate hazard: Ezh2 loss delays oligodendrocyte differentiation and Ezh1 compensates (mouse), so dual EZH1/EZH2 blockers are the highest-risk members. The arm is now reached from two different WWOX observations (glial cytokines and NRF2 tone), but through shared network edges, so it is not independent support.

    Conditional hypothesis: compound selectivity and cell activity are documented; the sign of the chain is contested inside its own reference list; no Wwox-deficient glial measurement (no ranked unit, so no evaluation depth applies: this is not a depth of zero)
    Decisive uncertainty
    The sign: falling cytokines reproduced by controls keeps the proposal conditional; rising cytokines reject the harm arm for this axis. The role of the cytokine change in the knockout is itself unmeasured. The compound is a substrate of efflux transporters in vitro and has no human exposure.

  • Class IIa-selective tool compound X against HDAC5 knockdown, with catalytic-dead and localisation-mutant HDAC5 rescue, a class-I-only inhibitor and an HDAC6 inhibitor as controls, in human neural cells new hypothesis generated by LEGEND conditional hypothesis, never presented as qualified
    Reference
    INV-16
    Question
    In human neural progenitors or neurons, does catalytic inhibition of class IIa HDACs lower the output of HDAC5 at SLC2A1 the way HDAC5 knockdown does, or does it leave it unchanged or raise it?
    Origin of the proposal
    Generated by LEGEND (proposal IT21P2-0006 and the HDAC5 to SLC2A1 chain, harm arm Q2); challenge CH-IT28-HDAC5-LEVER concluded NARROWED, not refuted, not confirmed; the vorinostat row is an earlier internal case of the same chain, reached before this premise was examined.
    Reason for the priority
    The HDAC5 to SLC2A1 thread rests on one muscle knockdown observation and has been carried as a limit, not a veto; the premise measurement it needs is the one open step of the IT28 challenge (WO-30). It sits at rank 7 because no neural line with the constructs is held and the readout does not change another row today.
    Available evidence
    Edge: HDAC5 to SLC2A1 traces to one origin, human primary muscle cells, where HDAC5 knockdown reduced GLUT1 expression (PMID 22991226, abstract level); the one drug tested there was pan-HDAC and was reported for GLUT4 only. Class IIa enzymes have very low intrinsic activity on standard substrates and repress largely as scaffolds; in neurons the separating experiments exist for HDAC4, not HDAC5; cardiomyocyte data show catalytic activity mattering for HDAC5 with the opposite sign (inhibition raises the output). Compound side: Compound X identity confirmed by full InChIKey (CHEMBL3110004); ChEMBL values from one paper, HDAC4 130, HDAC5 80, HDAC7 40, HDAC9 20 nM, in a recombinant catalytic-domain assay, cross-paper values vary and whether each was measured or quoted was not checked; whether compound X engages HDAC5 in cells at the cited exposures is not determined. Attribution gap of the pan-class comparator in this thread: vorinostat is held on main_target_weak_attribution (HDAC5 Ki 3600 against HDAC1 1.3 nM, fold 2769.2), so an effect of that compound would read as class I. Counter-premise carried in the generator: class I and pan-HDAC inhibition are signed adverse for oligodendrocyte maturation; for class IIa the CNS sign is unknown, the only myelin datum is a peripheral Schwann-cell double mutant of Hdac4 and Hdac5 (PMID 29472387, partial full text), and WWOX neuron-deleted mice are hypomyelinated. WWOX-system: HDAC5 mRNA nominally lower and SLC2A1 nominally higher in the P47T mouse, an mRNA association only; the human organoid shows SLC2A1 higher on transcript. IT32 reading of neural precedents: a catalytic-domain mutant of HDAC5 (two cysteines) lost deacetylase activity in vitro and abolished the effect of nuclear HDAC5 on one transcript and on a behaviour in rat nucleus accumbens (PMID 39923817, full text; no SLC2A1 or glucose readout, and loss of binding to another factor is not excluded), so the earlier statement that no neural catalytic arm exists is out of date; a catalytic-site mutant of the paralog HDAC4 rescued survival like the wild type in mouse cortical neurons (PMID 23141539); an inhibitor matched knockdown on neurite growth in neural cells but was inert where knockdown of HDAC7 acted (PMID 31572723; PMID 41962726, abstract only). Catalytic dependence is therefore specific to paralog, cell type and output. IT32 action-level reading (NB-3b): the premise source tested knockdown only, that is protein amount, and its pan-inhibitor arm names no GLUT1 result (abstract level); results for the paralog HDAC4 on GLUT1 go in both directions in non-neural cells; the direction of SLC2A1 in WWOX-deficient systems differs between the organoid, mouse brain and shWWOX neural cells, and no source reads SLC2A1 after HDAC5 manipulation in a neural cell.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    Conditional hypothesis: the edge has one muscle origin read at abstract level and the compound side is compiled data; a catalytic-domain mutant of HDAC5 exists in rat neurons for other outputs (PMID 39923817) but none reads SLC2A1 in a human neural cell (no ranked unit, so no evaluation depth applies: this is not a depth of zero)
    Decisive uncertainty
    Whether catalytic inhibition reproduces knockdown at SLC2A1 in a human neural cell: knockdown is not catalytic inhibition when the enzyme acts mostly as a scaffold. The premise is refuted if a catalytic-dead rescue restores SLC2A1 like wild type, if compound X leaves SLC2A1 unchanged while knockdown moves it and its cellular engagement of HDAC5 has been shown (without that, a null cannot separate scaffold function from non-engagement); a class-I-only inhibitor that reproduces the knockdown is ambiguous, because HDAC5 repression runs through HDAC3, and does not refute it alone; if inhibition raises SLC2A1 the lever inverts. Whether a change in SLC2A1 is favourable, compensatory or harmful in WWOX-deficient neural cells is itself unresolved, and a change in SLC2A1 is not a benefit. Potency of the broader HDAC compounds on HDAC5 cannot be compared until the methods of the three potency papers are readable (WO-29, data access blocked).
    Next test
    Step 1, no compound: HDAC5 knockdown in human neural progenitors or neurons reading SLC2A1 protein, glucose uptake and transcript, with rescue by wild type, a localisation mutant and a catalytic-site mutant. Step 2, only after cellular engagement of endogenous HDAC5 by the compound is shown with a readout specific to it (bulk histone acetylation is a weak reading for a class IIa enzyme): compound X, a class-I-only inhibitor (an ambiguous comparator) and an HDAC6 inhibitor as a chemotype comparator that needs its own qualification, not as a negative control. A myelin-relevant readout (oligodendrocyte-precursor differentiation, with and without neuron conditioning) is proposed in the IT29 P10 question record for the same experiment.
    Development feasibility
    Wet-lab measurement; no neural line with the constructs is held in the module. As a drug question, no statement of CNS exposure of the compounds is carried here. A compound result on this row would be read as a premise result, never as evidence that any compound works.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried on 2026-11-07: the IT28 P3 HDAC5 batch, the IT29 P10 question record, the IT29 P11 residue and identity records of compound X, the IT22 P6 reverse record and rows WO-29 and WO-30 of the open-questions map. A search of this module, not a statement about the literature. The vorinostat thread is an already-known internal reference, not an independent source of support.

Other open investigations, beyond the ten in the list (3)

The ten-row limit applies to the ordered list at the top, not to the queue of investigations: these stay open with their question, their position and their test. The position is a research priority, not the efficacy of an intervention, and being beyond the limit does not mean being less promising.

  • 6 (beyond the list limit) No compound: measurement of the parvalbumin interneuron population in neuron-targeted Wwox deletion, with cell number, identity and maturation, marker expression, intrinsic properties, synaptic input and circuit function read as six separate questions thread already known in WWOX measurement of a premise, without a compound
    Reference
    INV-15
    Question
    In the neuron-targeted Wwox-deletion mouse, is the lower Pvalb transcript due to fewer parvalbumin interneurons, to immature or altered identity, to lower marker expression in a normal number of cells, to changed intrinsic properties, to less synaptic input onto or from them, or to a circuit-level change, and which of these is measured per animal?
    Origin of the proposal
    Known in the WWOX system: the parvalbumin marker deficit is already a named need observation and the NP3A1 reopening trigger; the row restates the open question as six separable layers (IT13b, IT14 P1a, IT14 P1b, reopening table row NP3A1).
    Reason for the priority
    It decides whether any parvalbumin-directed pharmacology, positive modulation or another kind, can be thought about at all, and which of the inhibitory-hypofunction contrasts to run first. Its direction is not assumed: raising parvalbumin-cell activity is not taken to be the right direction. It enters at rank 6 as a premise measurement because the nucleus-level route was closed by the replicate structure of the deposit and what remains is a per-animal measurement.
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system, transcript: a lower Pvalb transcript in the neuron-targeted deletion in bulk hippocampus (log2 -1.70, GSE158681 S contrast, as quoted in IT13b) and about half that size in the nuclear data (GSE158684: Pvalb 70 against 37 UMI in 3182 against 2920 nuclei; nuclei Pvalb share ratio 0.59). GSE158684 holds one pooled library per arm (library and animal index absent; the paper states n = 1 per arm), so nuclei are not biological replicates and the GSM records of the series are not independent experiments; PV-class nuclei number 12 to 19 per arm under the producer rules, the independent recompute disagrees on the specific counts, and PV composition and Pvalb per cell are undecidable under every rule tried. Kcnc1 is lower in inhibitory nuclei (one pool, not a replicate result). Immature-neuron markers (Sox11, Dcx, Igfbpl1) are higher in knockout neurons in direction; the larger composition change is oligodendrocyte-class nuclei, about 3- to 5-fold fewer. Wwox also falls in glia-called nuclei, unexplained. Protein and function, from the need file: PV-positive counts reduced by 44 percent in the whole hippocampus of a systemic constitutive knockout (PMID 30290271) and spontaneous inhibitory current amplitude more than halved in layer II/III pyramidal neurons of the neuron-specific knockout (PMID 34634460; pooled events, not animals). Raw reads of the eight snRNA experiments (SRX9206272 to SRX9206279) carried NCBI status hup on 2026-10-31. A public conference abstract (poster 014, Curing the Epilepsies 2026 programme, NINDS; the whole abstract was read, abstract level) describes a programme that combines genetic mouse models, in vivo electrophysiology, ex vivo slice recordings, cell type-specific manipulations and targeted pharmacological modulation of neuronal activity in WWOX deficiency, and names parvalbumin interneurons as the population of interest; it reports no quantitative result, no molecule, no rescue and no target. IT33 reading of the glial signal (NB-4 pilot, independently audited): the deletion is neuron-targeted by design (Synapsin-Cre) and a lower Wwox transcript also appears in glia-annotated nuclei of one pool (oligodendrocyte-called 193 to 1 UMI, astrocyte-called 156 to 9: very small counts on the deleted side, one pool per arm, so a count of cells or a statement of glial loss is not supported); the readings are several and not exclusive (lower transcript in the annotated class, class definition and detectability, ambient RNA, recombination beyond the expected cells, a change of state or composition), and none is isolated. Two abstract-level sources describe the Synapsin-Cre line: germline recombination through male carriers (PMID 16419044) and non-cell-autonomous astrogliosis after a neuronal deletion of another gene (PMID 11297510); neither shows or excludes recombination in glia or in parvalbumin cells of this deletion.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    Premise measurement: the transcript deficit is observed in bulk and in one nuclear pool per arm; cell number, identity, intrinsic properties, synaptic input and circuit function are not measured at animal level by any file read here (no ranked unit, so no evaluation depth applies: this is not a depth of zero)
    Decisive uncertainty
    Which of the six layers moves, per animal. A lower transcript does not show fewer cells, lower activity or less inhibition; an absent change in GSE158684 is not evidence of no change; the oligodendrocyte-lineage shift could be consequence or cause of an excitation-inhibition change and the data cannot say which. Whether any parvalbumin-cell change is a deficit, a compensation or a delayed maturation is unresolved, so the need direction stays unresolved and no lever sign is derived. Whether recombination reaches parvalbumin cells, and glia, in this deletion is not known from any source read, and a reporter measured in another context does not measure the excision of Wwox in parvalbumin cells.
    Next test
    Per-animal parvalbumin cell counts by immunostaining in neuron-targeted Wwox deletion against Cre-only controls, at least 3 animals per arm (reopening condition (c) of NP3A1), read together with a maturation and identity marker panel in the same animals, and, where the data holders allow, intrinsic-property and inhibitory-input recordings from labelled parvalbumin cells and a circuit-level read. Alternatives that also reopen it: a deposited library or animal index for GSE158684, or an independent neuron-targeted deletion dataset with at least 3 animals per arm and a parvalbumin-enriched capture. The result is read as six separate rows (number, identity and maturation, marker expression, intrinsic properties, synaptic input, circuit function); a change in one is not carried to another. The per-animal measurement carries its own recombination read-out in the parvalbumin cells (reporter or genotype of the sorted or labelled cells) beside cell number, identity and marker expression; transcript, protein, activity, cell number and circuit function stay separate results.
    Development feasibility
    Not executable from this module: no animals or tissue are held and the raw reads are not public. Feasible only by data holders or a new dataset; nothing is sent to anyone from here. Zero-spend preparation is limited to fixing the readout table before any data arrive.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried on 2026-11-07: the IT13b, IT14 P1a and IT14 P1b records of this module, the NP3A1 row of the reopening table, and the need file; the public programme abstract of poster 014 (Curing the Epilepsies 2026, NINDS) was read at abstract level on 2026-11-07; it states a programme, not a result, so nothing quantitative is attributed to it. A search of this module, not a statement about the literature.

  • 7 (beyond the list limit) No compound: measurement of the role of the MYC rise in WWOX-deficient radial glia thread already known in WWOX measurement of a premise, without a compound
    Reference
    INV-17
    Question
    Is the MYC rise in WWOX-deficient radial glia a driver of the progenitor shift, a marker of a retained progenitor state, or a consequence of the cell-cycle shift?
    Origin of the proposal
    Known in the WWOX system: the observations are in the need record (O1 to O4); the row restates work-order question WO-33 as the one question behind the MYC-directed proposals.
    Reason for the priority
    555 of the 994 generated proposals end in a change of MYC, 314 in a harm arm and 241 in a protect arm (123 eligible for hand-over); whether any change of MYC is wanted depends on this role, so one measurement stands behind all of them and no MYC-directed lever is assumed beneficial.
    Available evidence
    WWOX-system, one organoid study (PMID 42397075): MYC is the most raised gene in knockout radial glia, which shift toward S and G2M; the fraction of SOX2-positive cells that are MYC-positive is raised in an engineered knockout and two patient-derived lines; one non-selective multi-kinase inhibitor reported to suppress Wnt and MYC lowers the SOX2-positive fraction in knockout organoids; neuron-promoter add-back raises deep-layer fractions. Transcript and cell fractions only: no protein, no manipulation of MYC itself.
    Solidity of the evidence (depth of reading)
    Premise measurement: the MYC rise is observed in one organoid study; its role is not measured. (no ranked unit, so no evaluation depth applies: this is not a depth of zero)
    Decisive uncertainty
    Driver, marker or consequence. If the MYC difference vanishes within cell-cycle and potency strata it is a marker and this observation alone justifies no lever; if genetic lowering of MYC moves the progenitor shift it is a driver, and the timing of any window is a separate question, not assumed to be prenatal only. MYC dose is two-sided in cortex and the record holds no safe pharmacological formulation for a developing compartment.
    Next test
    In WWOX-deficient and corrected isogenic organoids or radial-glia cultures: compare MYC within cell-cycle phase strata, then lower MYC by a genetic route with a second construct and read the progenitor fractions and the cell-cycle phase. No compound is needed for this step.
    Development feasibility
    Existing organoid systems; wet-lab measurement, not executable from this module.
    Novelty, within the verified scope
    Queried on 2026-11-07: the MYC need record, work-order entry WO-33, map row WO-33 and the stage S12 proposal table; a search of this module, not a statement about the literature. A scientific package on this role (NB-1) was in progress and is not used here.

What changes compared with IT21

Changes in IT22 in the way the generator uses what the repository already contained, with the count that demonstrates them. None of these rows is a scientific result on benefit.

  • A decision about one molecule no longer blocks every molecule that shares its target: it travels only as far as its own reason (the molecule's own potency or label stays with it; a refuted premise still closes the arm it belongs to). 69 proposals were blocked by the old rule; 24 stay closed (premise refuted), 45 are released to be judged on their own data, none promoted.
  • Potency is compared only between measures of the same type; unlike measures are kept side by side and never turned into an exclusion. 20 proposals blocked on weak target attribution became 5 (the verifier's lower-bound rule restored one); the cautious case (a pan-HDAC inhibitor 2,769-fold weaker at the listed target, same measure type) stays blocked.
  • Observations that no generator input carried now reach it: a new question on NRF2 tone (one organoid contrast, adjusted p above the deposit's own alpha, role unknown) produced 20 new conditional proposals (the axis itself was already a carded thread since IT10; the compound routes are new); a failed control (the second neural system's progenitor arm did not show WWOX lower) is attached to 71 proposals and a contested direction to 75 more, as carried limits (recorded in the output; removing their ordering term changes no hand-over); a cell-type marker set can no longer become a gene seed; a premise or class limit now travels wherever its edge or target appears in a chain, not only inside one cluster.
  • What did not change: the number of generated proposals from the old inputs (980, only selection changed), the absence of any qualified hypothesis, and the earlier retrospective result (WWOX seed identity not separable from matched random sets on the measured properties only).
  • Seven of eight new hand-overs were qualified on their own data and end inconclusive or conditional. Seven of the 16 hand-overs rest on one organoid deposit and six flip direction if the unknown role of their question flips; the main limit is not the number of candidates but missing measurements in a WWOX-deficient neural system.
  • IT23 tried six external capabilities on cases frozen beforehand (a knowledge graph, a network simulator, a protein-profile matrix, a signature search, disease-module discovery and a prediction model): none was adopted as a tool. One relation type became a carried limit: spontaneous seizure reports now appear as counter-evidence on 31 proposal rows and one hand-over, without moving any eligibility. The audit of the action table also found five suspect sign rows in LEGEND's own data. A simulation returned the assumed scenario, a profile matrix could not score the hand-over compounds and a signature search did not overlap with LEGEND's list: for these inputs the limit is the missing measurement of the cytokine axis and a larger qualified seed set, not the number of tools.
  • IT24 corrected and extended what the generator reads. After a source check, eight signed pairs (one compound on seven sirtuins and another on a caspase) were withheld: each rested on one review-table or trial-listing claim and no primary source supports a direction; no opposite sign was assigned, and none was the main link of any proposal. Chemical identity was recovered for 93 of the 115 rows that IT23 could not compare (89 firm), without merging by name; the comparison with a drug-signature search stays empty on 136 comparable rows. Splitting the calculation by target showed 32 conflicts between targets of one compound, almost all of them small, and 4 handed-over compounds with several favourable targets (two of them paralog pairs). New per-gene lists from public mouse data (a knock-in model and conditional deletions) are candidate pools, not findings. No position in this ranking changed, and none of these steps measures benefit or predictive accuracy.

Partial benefit: dedicated selection (3)

Which function one would want to improve, why, with which possible opposite effects and with which discriminating experiment. A selection curated by the agent, not a score: no row is qualified and the order is not a ranking; novelty, solidity of the evidence, WWOX relevance and feasibility remain separate.

  • Function to improve
    Oligodendrocyte maturation and myelination
    Why
    Neuron-driven developmental myelin deficit with precursors up and mature cells down; maturation block favoured over loss but not demonstrated (IT14).
    Candidate class
    Agonists of thyroid-hormone receptors (probe; a receptor-beta-leaning liver-directed agent only as isoform control)
    Possible opposite effects
    Thyroid-axis suppression and peripheral thyrotoxicosis at the effective mouse dose; seizure worsening reported in a few patients with prior seizures; premature differentiation.
    Discriminating experiment
    Seizure-free neuron plus precursor co-culture, WWOX-deficient versus corrected neurons, hormone-depleted medium, isoform control.
    Would close it
    Correction in both genotypes (non-specific), or no change, or correction only with the receptor-beta-leaning control.
    Novelty
    New molecule for LEGEND in a known thread
    Solidity of the evidence
    Conditional; human precedent is a hormone-entry defect without a neurodevelopmental endpoint
    WWOX relevance
    Moderate (pattern documented; no thyroid-axis datum)
    Feasibility
    Cell probe now; systemic use limited
  • Function to improve
    Glial inflammatory tone
    Why
    Cytokine transcripts up in two mouse Wwox-deficient preparations (one significant in the null hippocampus).
    Candidate class
    Blockers of the PRC2 methyltransferase EZH2, probe level; dual EZH1/EZH2 agents flagged highest-risk
    Possible opposite effects
    Net-negative on the myelin axis if both EZH1 and EZH2 are inhibited (oligodendrocyte differentiation blocked in mouse knockouts); cytokines rose after EZH2 suppression in tumour cells.
    Discriminating experiment
    Wwox-null versus wild-type glial cultures, the probe versus a second chemotype versus Ezh2 knockdown, histone mark and cytokine protein, with a parallel precursor-differentiation read.
    Would close it
    Cytokines rise or precursor differentiation falls.
    Novelty
    Known thread re-emitted with a corrected counter-evidence and a new hazard
    Solidity of the evidence
    Weak; sign contested; no measurement in a Wwox glia; brain exposure unmeasured
    WWOX relevance
    Moderate for the observation, none for the lever
    Feasibility
    In vitro tool compound only
  • Function to improve
    NRF2 tone and redox state
    Why
    Human knockout organoid shows a lower NFE2L2 transcript (0.75x), role unknown; the second system failed its control.
    Candidate class
    A topical agent acting on the AhR pathway as an in vitro probe after step 0; direct NRF2-activating drugs remain the carded probes
    Possible opposite effects
    AhR-pathway activation is adverse in neural precursors in toxin studies; the pathway-target transcript is higher while NFE2L2 is lower.
    Discriminating experiment
    Step 0: nuclear NRF2, NQO1 activity and a ROS reporter in isogenic WWOX-deficient versus corrected neural cultures at baseline and after an oxidative challenge; then probe versus NFE2L2 knockdown.
    Would close it
    No change at step 0 (axis not engaged), or AhR-dependent harm in precursors.
    Novelty
    New compound routes for the Q8 question; the NRF2 axis and its step 0 were already a carded thread since IT10; the molecule is in an earlier exclusion list
    Solidity of the evidence
    Weak; edge supported outside neural cells; no CNS exposure data for the topical drug
    WWOX relevance
    Low to moderate (one contrast, second system failed)
    Feasibility
    In vitro after step 0
