Where the new proposals come from

The generator produced 980 conditional proposals, 13 handed to qualification; of these 6 were qualified in depth in IT21 (1 kept conditional, 3 rejected with an informative outcome, 2 inconclusive). The compound-to-WWOX route produced 10 proposals: 2 kept conditional, 1 rejected with an informative outcome, 6 inconclusive; 5 were qualified in depth. Qualified hypotheses: 0. A conditional proposal remains a research question until there is a measurement in a system with altered WWOX.

What the generator now excludes (5)

Informative negative outcomes: they are not investigations to be funded. They concern the chain as it was written and do not say that a compound is inactive or that the biology is absent: what is not known is not ineffective. Each one states what would reopen it.

  • Lithium, inositol monophosphatase (IMPA1) as mediator
    Excluded
    Disfavoured, not ruled out (DISFAVOURED_BY_SIGN_PRECEDENT): that inositol monophosphatase inhibition contributes to the protection lithium gives in the Wwox seizure assay, or that this enzyme is a lever for it.
    Why
    The documented consequence of inhibiting this enzyme in rodents is a pro-convulsant effect that inositol reverses, which predicts aggravation, not the protection seen; the protection also appears in wild-type littermates, so it is not specific to WWOX loss. The precedent is an analogy from another model (the drug together with low-dose pilocarpine), not a measurement in the Wwox assay, so it disfavours the route and does not close the assay question; the same mouse paper also ran a pilocarpine model in Wwox mice, so the objection that the provocations differ is testable in the same system.
    Why
    Curated mechanism rows in ChEMBL list inhibition of both IMPA1 and GSK3A/B for lithium; the sign argument rests on three abstract-level references. The null/wild-type panels (N 6 vs 7 and 12 vs 8) show a lithium effect of about the size of the difference between the lithium and ethosuximide null controls.
    Reopens if
    Inositol add-back reverses the lithium effect in the Wwox-null assay (then the GSK3 attribution falls and the enzyme becomes a lever with an unexplained sign).
    Package
    IT21 P3b (G02)
  • DNA-damage-response inhibitors (ATR, CHEK1, WEE1, PARP1, ATM)
    Excluded
    That an inhibitor of the DNA-damage response is a lever for a WWOX-deficient developing brain.
    Why
    No scenario in the record makes over-activity of this response the harmful process; if the response is protective and already reduced, an inhibitor aggravates it. It is held as a harm flag, not a lever. Competence of the response in post-mitotic WWOX-deficient neurons is unmeasured.
    Why
    Path B reached these five genes through 80 signed inhibitor family-gene pairs, none named in a need; evidence for the competence deficit is non-neural (murine B cell and cell lines).
    Reopens if
    A WWOX-deficient neural measurement showing over-active checkpoint signalling that harms the cell.
    Package
    IT21 P3b (G06)
  • Nanatinostat, HDAC5 to SLC2A1
    Excluded
    The chain as written: that this inhibitor lowers SLC2A1 by acting on HDAC5 in a WWOX-deficient neural cell.
    Why
    Its strongest documented actions are on other deacetylases than the one the chain needs, the single reference for the edge is a knockdown in non-neural cells, so the attribution fails as written. (The two transcripts also move in opposite directions in the organoid, but that is a descriptive ratio that says nothing about enzyme activity and is not a reason.) This says nothing about whether the compound is inactive.
    Why
    HDAC1/2/3 about 3-7 nM against HDAC5 200 nM (a 67-fold difference) in ChEMBL activity rows; organoid HDAC5 0.81x with SLC2A1 2.67x.
    Reopens if
    HDAC5-specific lowering of SLC2A1 at concentrations that engage HDAC5, or class I inhibition changing SLC2A1 in either direction (then a different proposal).
    Package
    IT21 P4a (IT21P2-0006)
    ChEMBL register of the compound
    CHEMBL1801250
  • IOX1, KDM4C to HIF1A to HK2
    Excluded
    The chain as written: that this inhibitor lowers HIF activity without touching the HIF prolyl hydroxylases.
    Why
    In cells the compound stabilises HIF1alpha, the opposite of the intended effect, because concentrations that inhibit the intended demethylase overlap those that inhibit the prolyl hydroxylases; the intended target is also the least expressed family member in the WWOX-deficient organoid and absent in the human progenitor data. The route is the one that made another HIF-pathway agent a drop in IT9.
    Why
    Verbatim locator: the compound stabilised HIF1alpha at 0.2 mM relative to the control (Hopkinson 2013, partial full-text reading); ChEMBL PHD2 IC50 14.3-15 uM; KDM4C 11.7-17 cpm in the organoid.
    Reopens if
    A concentration window with H3K9me3 up, HIF1alpha unchanged and glycolytic genes down, reproduced by KDM4 knockdown (only if the role of HIF is first shown protective).
    Package
    IT21 P4a (IT21P2-0008)
    ChEMBL register of the compound
    CHEMBL1230640
  • CGI-1746, BTK to STAT3 to NPY
    Excluded
    The chain as written: that BTK acts in the NPY-producing cell of the WWOX-deficient systems that carry the seed.
    Why
    BTK is barely detected in the WWOX-deficient organoid and is not in the human progenitor table (a table-membership fact, not a measured zero), NPY is near zero where it was measured, both edges come from other cell types, and the compound has documented actions on unrelated proteins. A proposal can be unreadable where it was generated.
    Why
    BTK 0.07-0.50 cpm in organoid libraries, not in the hNPC table; NPY 0.05-0.12 cpm in knockout against 3.2-7.7 in wild type; published off-targets of this exact compound include the sigma-1 receptor and the proteasome.
    Reopens if
    BTK detected in the NPY-producing cell class with NPY following BTK knockdown; BTK only in microglia moves the idea to another proposal.
    Package
    IT21 P4a (IT21P2-0057)

Contribution of WWOX to the measurement. Retrospective measurement (IT21 P5, re-read in IT22): replacing the WWOX starting genes with randomly chosen genes of the same network size, the generator produces almost as many proposals (none of the 5 sets exceeds the 95th percentile of the closest comparisons). The conclusion holds only for the properties measured (number of proposals and membership of random sets): it is not the general conclusion that WWOX adds no value, because network interactions, cell-type-specific contrasts and premises about the role were not measured. It says nothing about prospective benefit, nor that the compounds listed are inactive. It reopens with a datum measured in the WWOX system that distinguishes the proposals.

A novelty holds only within the declared search scope: absence from a card or from a search does not mean “never studied”.

At a glance: where to start

Three questions, in the order in which it is useful to ask them: which biological threads already have something measured in WWOX, which interventions deserve a study and why, what is still missing. No entry is a probability of benefit or a ranking of treatments.

What type of evidence: three classes, always with the word next to the symbol

  • ●Measurement in WWOX a signed result of the intervention exists in a WWOX system (animal, cells, clinical cases); it may be weak or uncontrolled.
  • ◇Inference from outside WWOX no result in WWOX; the support or the counter-signal comes from other diseases, from safety or label data, or from a target assay.
  • ?Hypothesis nothing measured for this intervention on this need: the link is by mechanism only.
  • –Unclassified the type of evidence is not recorded: it is not a negative datum.

Rule: the class is read from the facts already computed for each card–need link; it is not a new score.

Biological threads: what supports, what weakens, what is missing

Each cell counts card–need links of the thread (an intervention linked to two needs counts twice). Order of the threads as in the register, not a ranking. Coverage counts needs of the thread with at least one observation in a WWOX system: it is not the share of disease treated.

Full reading: dates, perimeter and how to read the page

Data updated to: 2026-11-07 · Needs register of 2026-10-27 · Catalogue built on 2026-10-31T07:28:37Z · Perimeter: WWOX-DEE, reference genotype class; public literature and databases; no individual-level data. · Complete local version: includes third-party rows, not for redistribution.

How to read in four steps

  1. Choose a biological thread below.
  2. Look at the reason for the priority: the letter F, C or P.
  3. Open the candidate card for the six short answers.
  4. Read the evidence that is missing and the informative next step.

That a piece of information is missing (access, outcome, counter-evidence) does not mean that it is negative: it means that it has not been obtained.

The letters are reasons, not grades. Each link between candidate and need has its own letter; a card may have more than one, and there is no “best” one.

  • F1 favourable hypothesis, controlled WWOX readout. A favourable result in a WWOX system, read against an untreated group of the same genotype from a full or partial text, with no neutral, unfavourable or mixed results in WWOX alongside it, and with a next step named. It is a check of reading quality, not the measurement of an effect.
  • F2 favourable hypothesis, weak WWOX readout. A favourable result in a WWOX system, but uncontrolled (clinical cases, comparison with wild type only) or of limited depth or specificity, with no neutral or unfavourable results alongside it. The study serves to understand whether the signal is real.
  • F3 favourable hypothesis from the target, not proven in WWOX. The need has observations in WWOX systems, but the intervention has not been tested in WWOX; what exists comes from other diseases or from target assays, with no counter-signals. A next step is named.
  • C1 counter-evidence to be clarified, neutral or unfavourable WWOX readout. The only signed result in WWOX is neutral or unfavourable. The study serves to understand whether that result is real (dose, timing, genotype, depth of reading), not to confirm a hope.
  • C2 counter-evidence to be clarified, mixed WWOX readout. For this need, favourable results and neutral or unfavourable results in WWOX stand side by side. The study serves to understand which of the two holds.
  • C3 counter-evidence to be clarified, harm or neutral from outside WWOX. No signed result in WWOX; what exists outside WWOX (another disease, safety, label) is harmful or neutral, with no favourable signal alongside it. The study serves to understand whether this also applies to WWOX.
  • P1 missing premise, abstention. The card is an abstention: a datum is missing before a test can be designed. The missing datum is the first thing to obtain.
  • P2 missing premise, no next step. The card names no next step for this need, so no study can be proposed from it.
  • P3 missing premise, no favourable element recorded. No signed result of the intervention in WWOX and no counter-evidence to be clarified from outside WWOX; in addition, either every favourable support recorded for this need is missing, or every observation of the need in WWOX systems is missing. The card links the need by mechanism only; what is missing is stated in the criteria.

Two open possibilities, two separate dimensions

Broad recovery and partial benefit are not added up and are not compared. The Track (A: variant-independent; B: specific to the variant or the lesion) is a third, independent field. The 54 candidate–need links are all counted, each once, under the aim of the need; 4 of them link a card and a need with different aims, which is why the number of cards of an aim and the number of its links do not coincide.

Provisional ranking of interventions by priority of verification

A first, explainable and updatable ordering of the interventions that LEGEND has identified so far. It expresses scientific promise and the priority of the next study. It is not a validated prediction of clinical benefit, not a probability of success, not a therapeutic recommendation and not medical advice.

What it is not.
  • It is not a score: the groups are ordinal, have visible components and no hidden weight. No percentage is to be read as a probability of success.
  • It is not a ranking of safety or efficacy: access (prescription, over the counter, supplement) is only a description of source, with date and jurisdiction.
  • An intervention “still to be evaluated” is not “unpromising”: it is not at the bottom, it is in a separate group with the missing datum named.
  • Evidence from other diseases supports a mechanism or an experiment, never a result in WWOX. The same evidence is not counted more than once (preprint, article, database, articles that cite it).
How to read it
  1. The group (G1…GU) says how strong the reason is today to study the intervention further. Within a group there is a tie: the alphabetical order means nothing.
  2. Three views: general, broad and lasting recovery, partial benefit or bridge. The same intervention can sit in different groups because each view uses only the needs of its own aim; a strong result on symptoms does not cancel interest in a broad-recovery hypothesis, and vice versa.
  3. Track A/B (dependence on the variant or on the lesion) is a field separate from the group: depth of benefit and genetic applicability are different dimensions.
  4. An absent datum is “unknown”, not zero. Each count has its own denominator and is not a share of disease treated; linking more needs does not raise the group.

Three separate fields, readable on their own

  1. Biological promise: this is the group (G1…GU), computed from the positions; it contains neither the depth nor the priority of the next experiment.
  2. Depth of evidence: how much has been read and at what level (E0…E4); it does not enter the group.
  3. Priority of the next experiment (NX1…NX3): informative value = how much the next discriminating experiment would change a decision. It does not depend on how many times a candidate has been studied (a heavily studied candidate is not for that reason more promising, a little-studied one is not for that reason a discovery) nor on cost: cost and feasibility are a separate flag.

Priority groups

  • G1 Strongest case today, specific to WWOX (in the knockout mouse). A favourable result in a WWOX system, read against an untreated group of the same genotype, with no flag blocking the position and no neutral or unfavourable results alongside (position F1: a reading-quality filter on the rows that support the position, which may be a single row; not a measure of the effect and not a recovery after onset).
  • G2a Favourable but thin, WWOX outcome with limits of reading or design. A favourable result in a WWOX system with only limits of reading or design (uncontrolled, graph, a single experiment), with no neutral results alongside (position F2).
  • G2b Favourable but thin, specificity uncertain or untested. As G2a, but with a specificity flag: the effect also appears in wild type, or it is a tool compound, or a drug-by-genotype test is missing, or the wild-type arm is limited by the floor. Not having tested specificity is an unknown, never a clean reading; G2a versus G2b is not an order of efficacy (the source reports lithium better than ethosuximide, a single article, a single laboratory).
  • G3 Tried in a WWOX system: mixed, neutral or case-level results. Favourable and neutral or unfavourable results in WWOX side by side, or only a neutral result: the study serves to understand which one holds (positions C2, C1). The intervention is listed because it has been tried in a WWOX system, not because its favourable part is stronger than that of untried candidates; the class label describes the pertinence of the favourable part and is not a verdict.
  • G4a Hypothesis from the target, coherent action documented. No test of the intervention in WWOX; favourable support from outside WWOX; the need has observations in WWOX; an action coherent with the direction of the need is documented (position F3). The documented action does not by itself support the relevance to WWOX: the WWOX observation on the need may rest on another intervention.
  • G4b Hypothesis from the target, direction not established. As G4a but without a documented coherent action: direction uncertain, action unresolved or no identity in the catalogue (position F3).
  • G5 Weak pertinence or counter-evidence from outside WWOX. No signed result in WWOX, and a signal of harm or a neutral from outside WWOX with nothing favourable alongside, or a link by mechanism only (positions C3, P3).
  • GU Not yet orderable: missing premise. An abstention: a datum is missing before a test can be designed, or no linked need of this aim has a position. It is not a judgement of poor promise.

A selection lists at most ten interventions from groups G1, G2a, G2b, G3 and G4a, only when the evaluation supports them; never padded to reach ten. Ties stay whole. G4b and the following groups are listed separately.

IT7 exploratory information: the network and signature comparison (256 families) was neither detected nor excluded, deliberately excluded the curated cards and cannot by itself drive any position. No entry is ordered or reordered by it.

Matching direction, abstentions and limits EXPERIMENTAL

EXPERIMENTAL. For each need–intervention pair: the direction stated by the need, the documented action of the compound, the target level at which the source describes it, whether the relation is compatible, opposite or indeterminable, the reason for an abstention, the reference evidence with its independence, the datum that is missing and the useful next check.

Limits (to be read first).
  • Experimental capacity: retrospective comparison on a small reference chosen on purpose, not at random (32 pairs selected out of 25 compounds; 17 with a determinate reference, 11 from a functional measurement and 6 from a class-level attribution). No general accuracy and no superiority of one method over the other.
  • “Compatible” says only that the documented action goes in the direction that the need states. It is not research priority, not benefit in WWOX deficiency, and says nothing about safety or about whether that direction is the beneficial one.
  • Unknown does not mean negative: the bounded search found nothing, and that is a statement about the search, not about the compound.
  • An abstention leaves the row visible with action and reason: it removes a direction that the source record cannot support. On this selection it also removed a direction that the reference supports (a measurement on a single subunit): a field that would let a documented measurement restore it is still missing.
  • The reference was built by a single actor who knew the earlier labels; the module part is generated by the code. 8 of the 17 determinate references are independent of the sources with which the module was built; agreement on the others is not an independent confirmation.

32 pairs: 13 compatible, 3 opposite, 16 abstentions; reference: 13 compatible, 4 opposite, 9 indeterminable, 6 unknown. Agreement on the pairs with a determinate direction and reference: 13 of 13; no disagreement found on a selection built to find some. The correction of the group records changed 4 pairs.

How to read
  • Compatible: the action goes in the direction stated by the need. Opposite: it goes in the contrary direction (a reason for exclusion, not for interest). Indeterminable: the module abstains and says why.
  • The target level says what the source is talking about: a single protein, a family, a complex, a group of complexes or a gene listed without a stated level. An action written for a broad group is not attributed to a single gene when fewer than half of the components are targets of the module.
  • The reference is determinate (compatible or opposite), indeterminable (the evidence exists but not at the required resolution, or is binding only) or unknown (nothing found).

Source of each value: direction of the need: needs register; action, target level, label and reason: active search path, regenerated coverage; reference, type of measurement and independence: IT19 P5 comparison package; label before the group correction: module answers recorded in IT19 P5 before the correction. action_level_label_reason: coverage/associations.jsonl.gz (framework/scripts/repurposing_search.py, active path); before_fix: matching_it19_p5_20261102/module_answers_prefix.tsv (active path before the group-transfer guard); need_direction: needs/needs.json (intervention_direction); reference: matching_it19_p5_20261102/reference_it19_p5.tsv; selection: matching_it19_p5_20261102/selection.tsv

Passo 0 sulla premessa neurale; eventuale uso come sonda, non priorità clinica.
Misurare HIF-1α/HIF-2α proteina, compartimenti e ossigeno nei sistemi WWOX-deficiente e corretto. Se pertinente, perturbazione genetica prima/con la sonda e readout di funzione e vitalità.		Uso sistemico pediatrico nel SNC; separato dall’eventuale utilità ex vivo della sonda.
  • sconosciuto: Premessa HIF proteica e ruolo funzionale nel modello neurale — Il precedente WWOX-HIF è non neurale; RNA e propagazione di rete non misurano proteina né beneficio.
  • sconosciuto: Esposizione e tollerabilità pediatriche nel SNC — Non qualificate qui; struttura con allerta mustard, dati esterni e limiti tossicologici descritti in E-01.

Perché merita ricerca nonostante i requisiti irrisolti: Esposizione e tollerabilità pediatriche nel SNC sono sconosciute e la molecola ha un'allerta mustard, ma la premessa HIF si misura con perturbazione genetica senza il composto: la ricerca non dipende da quei requisiti.

Omaveloxolone
Attivatore di NRF2 (via KEAP1); potenza sul bersaglio nelle cellule neurali non misurata.		Sonda ex vivo in colture neurali isogeniche WWOX-deficiente e corretto che includano microglia o cellule simil-macrofagiche; il ruolo di ROS e citochine è sconosciuto, quindi il beneficio è condizionale.
Beneficio ipotizzato: Braccio citochine: abbassare Il6 e Il1b SE sono dannose E se esiste un compartimento che le esprime. Braccio redox: aumentare la capacità antiossidante SE le ROS sono dannose e il tono di NRF2 non è già massimo. Ruolo sconosciuto: entrambi condizionali.
nessun risultato WWOX attribuito a questa molecola. Nessun dato su NRF2, ROS o proteina citochinica in cellule neurali WWOX-deficienti di mammifero; il meccanismo citochinico viene da macrofagi di midollo (Il6 e Il1b giù, Tnf invariato). Un'etichetta senza la stringa «seizure» non è efficacia.
Perché è emerso
Grafo con segni, motore v4 con giunzione di membri: NFE2L2 -T(-)-> IL1B (arco terminale singolo, record con PMID letto) dai semi IL1B (cervelletto P47T) e IL6 (ippocampo null, l'unica citochina significativa); più il braccio redox aggiunto in IT10 P2.2.
Evidenza a sostegno
NRF2 attivato abbassa Il6 e Il1b e lascia Tnf invariato nei macrofagi (non neurale); ROS più alte nel moscerino con knockdown neuronale e nei MEF Wwox-null a passaggio tardivo; contenuto cerebrale simile al plasma nella scimmia. Nessun risultato in un sistema WWOX di mammifero.
Che cosa potrebbe confutarlo
Nel passo 0 nessuna differenza di ROS o di tono NRF2 e nessuna proteina citochinica sopra la soglia; attivazione che non cambia nulla mentre il knockdown di NFE2L2 non cambia nulla (asse inerte); un effetto che sopravvive al knockdown di NFE2L2 (fuori bersaglio); organoide senza cellule che esprimono citochine.

signed_network_propagation, mechanistic_context_transfer

Passo 0 (una o due settimane): dice se esiste un compartimento citochinico o un eccesso di ROS prima di qualsiasi test del composto; priorità di ricerca media.
Tono di NRF2, ROS e proteina IL-6/IL-1β nelle cellule WWOX-deficienti e corrette; poi attivazione con controllo di dipendenza da NFE2L2 (prima il knockdown di KEAP1; omaveloxolone e fumarato come due chemotipi) e knockdown di NFE2L2 come controllo di specificità.		Uso sistemico pediatrico per un effetto neurale WWOX-specifico. È DISTINTO dalla sonda ex vivo: verdetto sonda condizionale (via libera condizionato al passo 0), verdetto di sviluppo oggi non supportato.
  • sfavorevole: Età di indicazione e sicurezza pediatrica — Etichetta: indicato da 16 anni in su; sicurezza ed efficacia non stabilite sotto i 16 anni.
  • sfavorevole: Esposizione perinatale — Etichetta: nel ratto l'esposizione perinatale ha peggiorato la funzione neurocomportamentale della prole a tutte le dosi.
  • sconosciuto: Interazioni con induttori del CYP3A4 (molti antiepilettici) — L'etichetta chiede di evitare induttori forti o moderati; quali antiepilettici lo siano non è stato recuperato.
  • sconosciuto: Esposizione cerebrale libera e potenza nelle cellule neurali — Nella scimmia il contenuto cerebrale è simile al plasma ma l'induzione dei bersagli è modesta; ChEMBL non ha righe di potenza sul bersaglio; legame alle proteine elevato.

Perché merita ricerca nonostante i requisiti irrisolti: I requisiti di sviluppo sistemico sono sfavorevoli o sconosciuti, ma il passo 0 e il braccio genetico (KEAP1, NFE2L2) non usano il composto e rispondono alla domanda di ruolo per ogni leva Q5; il verdetto della sonda ex vivo è separato da quello dello sviluppo e non è annullato da esso.

Dasatinib
Inibizione del sito ATP di ACK1 (TNK2) e di SRC/ABL (non selettivo): sonda di meccanismo, non un trattamento.		Solo cellule con una banda WWOX (linee tumorali con ACK1 attivo, poi cellule neurali o organoidi con proteina residua); non si applica a Q230P finché il dato unico resta una non-rilevazione.
Beneficio ipotizzato: Emivita e livello stazionario di WWOX più lunghi SE la via Tyr287-ACK1 limita WWOX in quella cellula; solo quantità di proteina, la funzione non è prevista. Condizionale alla presenza di proteina.
nessun risultato WWOX attribuito a questa molecola. Nessun composto è stato dato a un sistema WWOX; le osservazioni ACK1-WWOX vengono da cancro (prostata, fegato) a livello di abstract; i valori ChEMBL ripetuti sono valori di letteratura riportati fra articoli, non repliche. Nessuna scheda e nessuna voce ordinata: la voce N12 non ha scheda. Dasatinib non è selettivo per ACK1 (34 bersagli più forti in un documento di profilazione) e bosutinib non è un chemotipo indipendente; il dato di knockdown è una linea di carcinoma epatocellulare, un costrutto, stato stazionario (IT11 P2.4).
Perché è emerso
Percorso non da grafo: Q1 non ha via di grafo; la ricerca complementare dei regolatori della stabilità della proteina trova ACK1, che fosforila WWOX in Tyr287 con poliubiquitinazione e degradazione (cellule LNCaP, abstract) e il cui knockdown alza WWOX in linee di epatocarcinoma (solo la direzione, abstract).
Evidenza a sostegno
Due sistemi tumorali indipendenti (prostata, fegato; solo abstract); inibitori catalogati con potenza nanomolare misurata su TNK2 (valori di letteratura riportati fra articoli, non repliche). Nessun dato in una cellula neurale o con variante.
Che cosa potrebbe confutarlo
Nessuna variazione di emivita o di livello di WWOX con l'inibitore o con il knockdown di TNK2 in cellule neurali o con variante; risposta a un solo inibitore (fuori bersaglio); nessuna proteina in Q230P; ACK1 non attivo nei neuroni; sensibilizzazione all'apoptosi con ACK1 inibita nei neuroni granulari cerebellari di ratto.

residual_product_rescue, mechanistic_context_transfer

Prima il testo completo di Mahajan 2005 e il dato sul destino della proteina; poi, se c'è proteina, il confronto dasatinib, bosutinib e knockdown di TNK2.
Emivita (cicloesimide) e livello stazionario di WWOX con composto, knockdown di TNK2 come comparatore genetico, WWOX Tyr287Phe come controllo insensibile; regola di concordanza fra i due inibitori e il knockdown; lettura di funzione separata dalla quantità. Bracci distinti per chemotipo e bracci genetici (Tnk2-null, un secondo shRNA con mRNA di WWOX) come primo passo.		Uso di un chinasi-inibitore antineoplastico multi-bersaglio in un contesto neurale pediatrico, distinto dalla sonda in cellule.
  • sconosciuto: Proteina WWOX presente nel sistema di interesse — Per Q230P il dato unico è una non-rilevazione con un limite di sensibilità; senza proteina la leva non si applica.
  • sconosciuto: Esposizione e tollerabilità nel SNC — Non valutate; entrambi i composti sono antineoplastici multi-bersaglio.
  • sconosciuto: ACK1 espresso e attivo nei neuroni — Solo RNA da atlante, in tutti i tessuti; la proteina non è stata controllata.

Perché merita ricerca nonostante i requisiti irrisolti: Presenza di proteina, esposizione nel SNC e tollerabilità sono sconosciute: non tolgono la domanda su cosa limiti l'emivita di WWOX in una cellula che ha una banda, misurabile in vitro con la regola di concordanza. La voce resta senza scheda finché non c'è il testo completo di Mahajan 2005.

Casi approfonditi a confronto

Each case answers the same questions. The level says what kind of support exists, not how promising the compound is: no level is an efficacy score and the coverage of a pathway describes connections, not a share of disease treated. A functional measurement may be non-specific (for example reducing seizures also in wild type). Unknown does not mean negative.

  • ○ Catalogued the compound is only in the catalogue, with no documented link to a need
  • ◔ Linked documented action on a target linked to a need; no quantitative reading, or only non-quantitative clinical observations
  • ◑ Deepened identity, action and quantitative potency read and graded; no functional measurement in a relevant system
  • ● Functional measurement exists a functional measurement exists in a relevant system, stated in the case; it may be non-specific or may not distinguish genotypes; it is not proof of benefit
  • ◇ Still hypothetical hypothesis without a measurement for the specific step

GluN2B negative allosteric modulators at the ifenprodil site: ifenprodil and Ro 25-6981 as tools, radiprodil as clinical-stage comparatorSame slice preparation; potencies from human or rat recombinant receptors in oocytesBursts are d-APV-sensitive; NMDAR current not measured (so the GluN2B share f at this age is unknown).Two independent papers compiled in one review: ifenprodil 110 vs 39,500 nM (359x, human, 3 uM glycine, -40 mV) and Ro 25-6981 9 vs 52,000 nM (5,778x, rat context); one source for the mouse layer II/III ifenprodil sensitivity exists at abstract level only.GluN2B over GluN2A by about 70-fold (eliprodil) to 360-fold (ifenprodil) and 5,800-fold (Ro 25-6981) across tools and conditions; the stated reduction of the isolated current is an UPPER BOUND, sum of f_i x Emax_i x occupancy_i.

1. AAV9-delivered human WWOX (gene addition) gene therapy / gene modality lead known before IT9 G1

G1 · Strongest case today, specific to WWOX (in the knockout mouse)

not a product listing (gene-based modality); access UNKNOWN
Context
mouse; constitutive Wwox deletion (targeted-deletion allele, FVB); complete_fulltext_read
Main reason
Strongest WWOX-specific case today (in the mouse null): lead position F1 on NEED-WWOX-GENE-ADDITION. On that need: 4 benefit, 2 partial_benefit, 2 unquantified; outside WWOX 0 favourable and 0 null or harm. Mechanism: modality acting on WWOX dosage or transcript itself: no drug-target identity applies (not a compound question); coherence with the need is by design, not by a catalogue action.
Best pertinent evidence
carrier of the position, DR-AAV-SURV-HD: proportion of animals alive over time: increase (+6 other favourable WWOX-system assertion(s) on the unit)
Main limit
audit_repair_not_rejudged; high_dose_arm; n=30_vs_KO_n=10 | G1 rests on a single pertinence row: high-dose survival, n=30 vs untreated knockout n=10, flag audit_repair_not_rejudged; the audit repair on that row is still to be adjudicated before any claim-level use. Prevention or early-window result in a null mouse (injection P0 to P5; later intervention not explored); one laboratory (two papers, shared senior author). | External precedent (not WWOX): seizure endpoints after onset are split by restoration mode and endpoint identity; myelin sheath structure after onset in a neuron-driven lesion is unmeasured; a post-onset null on spike-wave rate alone would be consistent with part of the precedent set and must not be pre-registered as expected.
Counter-evidence (claims from the needs record)
  • Rescue is not normalisation: unmyelinated axons per field remain about 52 versus about 26 in wild type.
  • The neuron-promoter vector corrected neuronal function without correcting radial-glia abnormalities (organoid arm); SATB2 mRNA overshoots wild type up to about eleven-fold in treated organoids.
  • No ceiling is measured and no tumour-surveillance or overexpression-toxicity endpoint exists in the mouse study; applied recombinant WWOX lowered viability of human ESC-derived cortical neurons in a preprint. More is not safer.
Notes
Graph coverage (IT11 P2.1): gene addition is out of the method (a modality, not a molecule), so the graph is silent on it by construction; its WWOX-system result is not a graph result. The five phenotype leads are development inputs, not an independent validation.
In the other aim
G3 Partial benefit or bridge: position C2
Needs and pathways
Systemic metabolic decompensation [C2; effect observed in the relevant system]; Restoring WWOX protein in neurons by adding the gene [F1; effect observed in the relevant system] 2 linked needs out of 23: a count of links, not a share of disease treated; it does not raise the group.
Next useful experiment or check
Does an intermediate vector level separate a threshold from a gradient, and is the benefit only prevented inside the first days of life or also recovered when treatment follows onset? No study has measured the phenotype at the day of injection. [verificare un'ipotesi]
Feasibility of the next step (separate from the biological promise)
Wet-lab work in a Wwox-null mouse by a laboratory that has the vector; none known in this repository; the source laboratory is one group (the two papers share a senior author). Whether the vector is obtainable: not known. External preceden…

already at the top group; it holds while no null, unfavourable or mixed WWOX-system result appears beside it | further questions: an overexpression or ceiling endpoint and a tumour-surveillance endpoint (none exists); whether the organoid radial-glia and SATB2 findings (same-laboratory human-system results, PMID 34268881 and 42397075, context only, not separate positions) hold Quantified myelination would add a controlled row on the same need; a failure would move the card to C2 by rule; a treated-after-onset arm would show whether the word recovery may be used for that endpoint. A post-onset arm that moved a circuit readout but not quantified sheath structure would match the precedents. The reverse pattern would be the first of…
It could fall if
a signed null, unfavourable or mixed result beside the favourable rows lowers the group by one step; a counter-evidence group (C1/C2) is reached only when the null stands as the lead; for a thin readout, a failed replication or a drug-by-genotype test showing the effect in wild type too moves it down within the group
It could leave the selection if

Context
mouse; Wwox -/- constitutive null; complete_fulltext_read
Main reason
Favourable but thin, specificity uncertain or untested: lead position F2 on NEED-T-TYPE-CALCIUM. On that need: 1 benefit; outside WWOX 0 favourable and 1 null or harm. Mechanism: 1 catalogue family(ies); L2 over 2 (family, need) cell(s): 1 coherent, 1 direction_unresolved.
Best pertinent evidence
A-ETX-1: PTZ-provoked behavioural seizure score, late phase of the hour (graphical reading): decrease
Main limit
control_variability_comparable_to_effect; endpoint_downstream_of_need; graphical_reading; late_phase_only; no_T_type_measurement; no_drug_by_genotype_test | same paper and laboratory as lithium (PMID 32000863), one experiment, i.p., one PTZ dose, effect confined to the late phase; no wild-type or drug-by-genotype test and the wild-type arm is floor-limited, so absence of a wild-type effect is unknown, not clean; the paper reports lithium better than ethosuximide | ethosuximide T-type potency in ChEMBL is above 5 mM (screening bound) or 600 uM with target unspecified, against a labelled plasma range of about 283 to 708 uM: T-type mediation of the observed effect is not measured
Counter-evidence (claims from the needs record)
  • IT12 P2.2 figure audit (dated 2026-10-31, PMID 37275776 Fig 7B, image viewed): the stored statement that the GIRK2 crossings lie inside the therapeutic band is wrong on one clause. In oocytes the GIRK2 homomer activated by Gbeta-gamma is half-maximally inhibited at about 0.03 to 0.06 mM, about 4 to 8 times BELOW the shaded band (about 0.25 to 0.9 mM), while the brain-predominant GIRK1/2 plus Gbeta-gamma channel crosses at about 0.4 to 1 mM, inside it (partial block, about 20 to 60 percent). So a measured non-T-type target exists at labelled exposure, and the wording 'T-type potency is weak against the labelled range' is not the whole story: the ethosuximide result in the WWOX mouse (PTZ seizure score) cannot be attributed to T-type mediation. An oocyte datum, not a WWOX mechanism; the authors say neuronal GIRK2 homomer abundance is unknown. In a genetic absence model the relay-neuron T-type current is smaller than control and the burst-threshold difference follows Ih (PMID 24953239 Figs 5 and 6). No group or member evidence changes.
  • IT13 P3a (2026-10-31): ethosuximide's attribution to T-type channels is not supported by any measurement in Wwox tissue: the catalogue mechanism record lists T-type only, the source paper's own oocyte data show GIRK block near the labelled band (a GIRK route would predict the opposite sign; prior knowledge), the two PTZ-alone null cohorts of the figure differ by about the size of the drug effect, no interaction test, and P17 Cacna1g/h/Kcnj6 transcripts are inside the control-line background. The late-phase effect stays one experiment in one laboratory; the group is unchanged.
Notes
the one outside-WWOX harm row is class-level (other T-type blockers lowered progenitor viability; ethosuximide was not tested), not ethosuximide data Graph coverage (IT11 P2.1): the generation graph has no way to speak about this molecule: its signed targets (the T-type channel genes CACNA1G, CACNA1H, CACNA1I) are sink or isolated nodes of the signed network, so no seed set can reach them. The absence of a graph row is not evidence about ethosuximide, and the lead was a development input of the phenotype-first path, not an independent validation of the graph. IT28 (compare_it28_p9_20261105): the added value over the untreated control is an interaction-tested late-phase effect only; the comparison that would attribute an effect to T-type block is one specificity design (both genotypes treated, concurrent control, drug-by-genotype term) and then a single attribution arm, either a nanomolar pan-Cav3 blocker with measured brain exposure or a Cacna1g occlusion arm. A second antiseizure agent serves as a nonspecificity reference only; its sign in a Wwox pup assay is UNKNOWN. IT29 (phenotype_first_it29_20261105/case2_lesion_conditional_it29.tsv): no corroboration in epilepsy-model screens of other genotypes; the T-type thread keeps its place on the single pup experiment
Needs and pathways
Control of seizures and spasms as a symptomatic need [F2; effect observed in the relevant system]; Ethosuximide sensitivity of the provoked seizure in Wwox loss [F2; effect observed in the relevant system] 2 linked needs out of 23: a count of links, not a share of disease treated; it does not raise the group.

Main limit
control_variability_comparable_to_effect; endpoint_downstream_of_need; graphical_reading; late_phase_only; no_T_type_measurement; no_drug_by_genotype_test | same paper and laboratory as lithium (PMID 32000863), one experiment, i.p., one PTZ dose, effect confined to the late phase; no wild-type or drug-by-genotype test and the wild-type arm is floor-limited, so absence of a wild-type effect is unknown, not clean; the paper reports lithium better than ethosuximide | ethosuximide T-type potency in ChEMBL is above 5 mM (screening bound) or 600 uM with target unspecified, against a labelled plasma range of about 283 to 708 uM: T-type mediation of the observed effect is not measured
Counter-evidence (claims from the needs record)
  • IT12 P2.2 figure audit (dated 2026-10-31, PMID 37275776 Fig 7B, image viewed): the stored statement that the GIRK2 crossings lie inside the therapeutic band is wrong on one clause. In oocytes the GIRK2 homomer activated by Gbeta-gamma is half-maximally inhibited at about 0.03 to 0.06 mM, about 4 to 8 times BELOW the shaded band (about 0.25 to 0.9 mM), while the brain-predominant GIRK1/2 plus Gbeta-gamma channel crosses at about 0.4 to 1 mM, inside it (partial block, about 20 to 60 percent). So a measured non-T-type target exists at labelled exposure, and the wording 'T-type potency is weak against the labelled range' is not the whole story: the ethosuximide result in the WWOX mouse (PTZ seizure score) cannot be attributed to T-type mediation. An oocyte datum, not a WWOX mechanism; the authors say neuronal GIRK2 homomer abundance is unknown. In a genetic absence model the relay-neuron T-type current is smaller than control and the burst-threshold difference follows Ih (PMID 24953239 Figs 5 and 6). No group or member evidence changes.
  • IT13 P3a (2026-10-31): ethosuximide's attribution to T-type channels is not supported by any measurement in Wwox tissue: the catalogue mechanism record lists T-type only, the source paper's own oocyte data show GIRK block near the labelled band (a GIRK route would predict the opposite sign; prior knowledge), the two PTZ-alone null cohorts of the figure differ by about the size of the drug effect, no interaction test, and P17 Cacna1g/h/Kcnj6 transcripts are inside the control-line background. The late-phase effect stays one experiment in one laboratory; the group is unchanged.
Notes
the one outside-WWOX harm row is class-level (other T-type blockers lowered progenitor viability; ethosuximide was not tested), not ethosuximide data Graph coverage (IT11 P2.1): the generation graph has no way to speak about this molecule: its signed targets (the T-type channel genes CACNA1G, CACNA1H, CACNA1I) are sink or isolated nodes of the signed network, so no seed set can reach them. The absence of a graph row is not evidence about ethosuximide, and the lead was a development input of the phenotype-first path, not an independent validation of the graph. IT28 (compare_it28_p9_20261105): the added value over the untreated control is an interaction-tested late-phase effect only; the comparison that would attribute an effect to T-type block is one specificity design (both genotypes treated, concurrent control, drug-by-genotype term) and then a single attribution arm, either a nanomolar pan-Cav3 blocker with measured brain exposure or a Cacna1g occlusion arm. A second antiseizure agent serves as a nonspecificity reference only; its sign in a Wwox pup assay is UNKNOWN. IT29 (phenotype_first_it29_20261105/case2_lesion_conditional_it29.tsv): no corroboration in epilepsy-model screens of other genotypes; the T-type thread keeps its place on the single pup experiment

Inventory: from the catalogue to the ordered interventions

We start from the catalogue; a compound present only in a database has, by definition, no WWOX rationale. The families merge salts and relatives by structural key; twins by name are not merged and do not inflate the positions, because each intervention is a single entry.

ClassEntries of the ranking
EVALUATED AND ORDERABLE16at least one linked need has a favourable position (F1, F2 or F3)
EVALUATED WITH WEAK PERTINENCE OR COUNTER-EVIDENCE5evaluated at card level but every position is counter-evidence or a link by mechanism only
STILL INSUFFICIENTLY EVALUATED16each card is an abstention or indicates no step: a datum is missing before a test; it is not placed at the bottom
EXCLUDED FROM A SPECIFIC COMPARISON, WITH REASON32an endpoint axis with no candidate: it is not an intervention and there is nothing to order

ACK1 (TNK2) and ITCH as regulators of WWOX protein stability (Q1 complement): dasatinib and bosutinib as paired ACK1 probes, conditional on WWOX protein being present
N12 · target_class
STILL INSUFFICIENTLY EVALUATEDE1Q1 complement (IT10 P2.3): Q1 has no graph route, and a complementary search for regulators of WWOX protein stability yields one usable slice, a mechanism experiment on protein level only. ACK1 over-expression with an engineered activated kinase phosphorylates WWOX, predominantly at Tyr287, and is followed by polyubiquitination, mostly in HEK293T cells (endogenous Wwox ubiquitination in LNCaP appears only after MG-132, and the ubiquitin assays are under MG-132 pretreatment); degradation as a consequence of Tyr287 phosphorylation is inferred, not shown (PMID 16288044, Mahajan 2005, full text read at the original on 2026-10-31, receipt FTR-20261031-16288044-01, Figs 1-8 inspected, supplement unavailable: phosphorylation and polyubiquitination are shown in overexpressed non-neural cells with an engineered activated kinase; Tyr287 is the predominant, not the only, phosphorylation site by pTyr signal; the paper does not show that Y287F resists ubiquitination or degradation, Fig 5E has no lane without activated Ack1 and one time point, Fig 5F shows MG-132-revealed ubiquitination and no level rescue so the proteasomal route is inferred, and no ACK1 inhibitor is measured against WWOX); ACK1 shRNA raised WWOX in one HCC line (MHCC-97H), one construct versus scrambled, steady state only (PMID 25738261, full text read 2026-10-30 in IT11 P2.4; it supports ONLY the direction 'knockdown raises WWOX', not the Tyr287 or ubiquitin route). Two catalogued ATP-site inhibitors with measured TNK2 potency (dasatinib, bosutinib; multi-target SRC/ABL kinase inhibitors that share SRC/ABL targets and bind SRC tighter than ACK1: concordance of the two does not identify ACK1 and bosutinib is not an independent chemotype; IT11 P2.4) would be paired probes with the concordance rule (agreement with TNK2 knockdown, a response to one only is off-target); the repeated ChEMBL values (bosutinib 2.7 nM, dasatinib Kd 5.6 and 6.0 nM) are literature values carried between papers, not replicates. CONDITIONAL on WWOX protein being present: no model is shown to have a variant protein above the assay floor, and a band not detected in the Q230P fibroblast blot does not separate a protein made and cleared from one never made, so the substrate is UNCONFIRMED, not excluded. Nothing predicts function; ITCH raises WWOX half-life but has no compound. COUNTER-EVIDENCE: the ACK1 observation is cancer-cell over-expression (prostate, liver); no Tyr287 change in serum-starved MEFs; MG-132 raised neither wild type nor the P252A or P282A constructs, so a proteasomal route is not shown in the only variant system, whereas chloroquine and NH4Cl restored P252A and chloroquine also prevented its degradation under cycloheximide (a main-text sentence of PMID 41124647), which supports a lysosomal route; ACK1 inhibition sensitised rat cerebellar granule neurons to apoptotic stress (PMID 37263460, abstract); broad kinase inhibitors shift WWOX phospho-forms in cancer cells. The TNK2 missense that abolishes NEDD4 binding in a family with infantile-onset epilepsy (PMID 23686771, abstract) is NOT counter-evidence for lowering ACK1: the abstract gives no kinase-activity direction and it is one family. CNS exposure and tolerability of both agents were not assessed. Not carded: R3 is satisfied as to the source (Mahajan 2005 and the HCC paper both read) and shows the decisive datum is absent from both, so the unit still waits for a datum that no source holds: a WWOX level, half-life or ubiquitination read after an ACK1-directed intervention including Tyr287Phe, with the no-activated-ACK1 arm and the route arm (ack1_it13_mahajan_20261031/controls_ack1_it13.tsv). Substrate census (IT12 P1-main, 2026-10-31; priority NOT raised, scope narrowed): in published neural WWOX models only wild-type cells (hESC/iPSC neural stem cells and organoids), AAV add-back (wild-type sequence) and one SCAR12 genotype (two siblings, each homozygous for ONE variant, c.1114G>C p.Gly372Arg, a C-terminal missense; its result does not extend to Q230P or to missense variants in general) show any band; the SCAR12 band is faint (0.1 to 0.3 of an unrelated wild type, one membrane) and on a second blot (EV6F, GAPDH loading control; the first blot EV1N uses HSP90) it is similar to the knockout lanes, so it is not shown above the assay floor; the WOREE lines show no visible band (EV1M, where wild-type band saturation is clear; it is mild in EV1N and EV6F). Q230P fibroblast blot: there is a negative control (CRISPR knockout clones) and three positive cancer/HEK lines, but no healthy fibroblast control and no heterozygote lane, and the epitope of the antibody sc-20528 is not stated. lde/lde rat: a trace frameshift product with a newer antibody (HPA050992, aa 32 to 110); that the earlier 'null' call depended on the antibody is the authors' hypothesis, not a demonstrated fact, and the paper gives 'lower mobility' in the Results but 'slightly heavier' in Discussion and legend (46.2 kDa; frameshift product predicted +0.8 kDa). Conclusion: no model has a protein level shown above the assay floor; the substrate for a stability lever is UNCONFIRMED, not excluded; the G372R line is the one model to retest first, after gate G0 (two antibodies, knockout floor). Q1 unit text: the reference class allele Q230P has no band in one non-neural line, no matched control, antibody sc-20528; made-and-cleared versus not made is open; the only neural lines with a missense allele are G372R (SCAR12) and G137V (WCH, iPSC only). the reopenable searches R1 to R7 in triggers.tsv (rows R*_q1_complement): above all R3 (full text of Mahajan 2005 and the HCC paper), R2 (WWOX protein or half-life after ACK1 inhibition or TNK2 loss in a neural or variant-allele cell) and R1 (whether the Q230P protein is made and cleared); a card and a mechanism-probe unit would be created only after R3 or R2—
BMP pathway ligands (recombinant BMP-7 eptotermin alfa and BMP-2 dibotermin alfa) as a layer-identity lever
N14 · target_class
STILL INSUFFICIENTLY EVALUATEDE1Engine output on a recovery-defined seed pair (BCL11B down, SATB2 down; the two layer-identity readouts that neuron-stage WWOX add-back restored in WOREE organoids, PMID 42397075 Fig 6): 127 of 12,560 examined families reach the two seeds, the top two (Z 4.9 and 4.4) are recombinant ligands, with 500 null draws on 2 seeds. This is an engine statement, not evidence of an effect; the layer markers are one readout and firing a separate one (they dissociate in SCAR12). A title-level counter-datum: WWOX loss raises TGF-beta/BMP2 signalling in a pancreatic cancer line (PMID 36572673, title only). Recombinant protein ligands are systemic-development poor candidates. Not advanced; no card. a gene-level add-back or knockout contrast that moves BMP-pathway genes in WWOX-deficient neural cells (E-MTAB-14792 if released), or a BMP arm with a layer-marker read-out in a WWOX organoid—
Digoxin (cardiac glycoside; HIF1A-axis inhibitor in cells) on the null-mouse glycaemia readout
N15 · target_class
STILL INSUFFICIENTLY EVALUATEDE1A candidate gap in the phenotype-first list: in the Wwox-null mouse digoxin raised blood glucose within 40 minutes (n=3, no wild-type arm attested; the printed dose of 100 mg/kg i.p. is flagged implausible), a readout the vector add-back also recovers longitudinally (glycaemia normal from P20, PMID 42422765). Same endpoint class, a different measure (acute versus longitudinal), systemic not neural, one source relayed from the repository census (PMC body empty on 2026-09-22), and digoxin acts through Na/K-ATPase with HIF1A inhibition as a side pharmacology. A cardiac glycoside is generally understood to have a narrow therapeutic window (general pharmacology, not checked here). Not a neural benefit and not a candidate; recorded so the gap in the phenotype-first list is visible. a replicated null-mouse glycaemia arm with a wild-type comparator and a verified dose, or a neural or neuron-level readout for the HIF1A axis in WWOX-deficient cells—
Kv7 (KCNQ2/3) openers: ezogabine as an ex vivo probe, azetukalner as the clinical-stage member
N13 · target_class
STILL INSUFFICIENTLY EVALUATEDE1IT14 P3 re-labelled this proposal as the counter-hypothesis (refuter) arm of the inhibition question: the heterozygote shares the input-resistance change and is intermediate in resting potential yet bursts in 4 of 23 slices against 36 of 42, so a graded intrinsic change alone does not account for the difference in bursting unless a threshold effect is invoked (the 1.9 mV heterozygote-versus-knockout gap in resting potential was not tested). A proposal of IT13 P3a, not carded: the basis is a depolarised resting potential reported in a neuron-deleted slice study (about 5 mV, Breton 2021, relayed) and, weakly, Kcnq2/Kcnq3 transcripts lower in the P17 deposits; the Kcnq2 difference sits inside the control-line background (not interpretable at n of 2 to 4) and direction of a channel mRNA is not benefit. A reduced channel number lowers the ceiling of an opener. Identity from ChEMBL only (ezogabine CHEMBL41355 phase 4, KCNQ opener; azetukalner CHEMBL5095264 phase 3, no mechanism record in ChEMBL); ezogabine withdrawal and metabolite statements are prior knowledge and not verified here; paediatric exposure, label and safety were not searched. Ex vivo probe use only, development not assessed; no WWOX result exists for any Kv7 agent. resting potential and the XE991-sensitive current in knockout versus control neurons, then an opener effect on bursts with the bath composition stated (reopen trigger NP3A3)U21
Benzodiazepine-site positive modulation of fast GABA-A inhibition: clobazam and its metabolite N-desmethylclobazam as ex vivo probes (compensation of a measured inhibitory loss)
N16 · target_class
STILL INSUFFICIENTLY EVALUATEDE1A function-first probe-level hypothesis of IT14 P3, not carded. Generated by the largest knockout-specific effect stated in Breton 2021 (sIPSC amplitude about -52 percent in layer II/III pyramidal cells of the neuron-deleted neocortical slice); inferred: that the loss is receptor-limited rather than release-limited and that a potentiator can restore enough charge (the knockout amplitude is about 48 percent of control and in recombinant receptors the metabolite's maximal potentiation is 143 to 253 percent of the GABA response at EC10 in rat HEK293 cells and 203 to 270 percent at EC20 in human oocytes, readouts that are not directly comparable). Counter-evidence and limits: heterozygote-versus-wild-type inhibition is not reported and the heterozygote bursts in 4 of 23 slices; excitatory-gain and intrinsic (input resistance, sag) readings stay live; sIPSC was recorded with a KCl internal solution; subtype selectivity of both agents is disputed across three primary papers (efficacy ratio alpha2/alpha1 of the metabolite 1.77 in rat HEK293 cells, a comparison that confounds the alpha subtype with the beta subunit (alpha1beta2gamma2 against alpha2beta3gamma2); non-selective in human oocytes, modest alpha2 affinity preference in binding); no GABAergic drug has been tested in any WWOX preparation. Identity: ChEMBL CHEMBL70418 (clobazam) and CHEMBL2260842 (N-desmethylclobazam, listed as NOR-CLOBAZAM); label and exposure facts are not carried here; ex vivo probe use only, no systemic or paediatric claim and no dose. not a precondition for a class-level ex vivo arm; E0 locus data, heterozygote-versus-wild-type sIPSC data or a same-system subtype comparison change how a result is attributed (triggers NP3P1 to NP3P3)—
GluN2B negative allosteric modulators at the ifenprodil site (ifenprodil and Ro 25-6981 as tools, radiprodil as clinical-stage comparator) as ex vivo probes of the NMDAR contribution to slice bursting

STILL INSUFFICIENTLY EVALUATEDE2IT15 Q-A target-first search (ChEMBL, graded same-document comparisons) with independent verification. Generated by the d-APV sensitivity of the neuron-deleted slice bursts together with the unmeasured NMDAR current. Pharmacology: GluN2B over GluN2A about 360-fold (ifenprodil, human, 3 uM glycine, -40 mV) and about 5,800-fold (Ro 25-6981, rat context), two independent papers compiled in a review with different stated conditions; the expected fall of the isolated current is an upper bound (incomplete inhibition, triheteromers); radiprodil has only complex-level values. Limits: the GluN2B share of the slice NMDAR current is unmeasured; pore blockers show no subunit selectivity detected; no GluN2B NAM was tested in any WWOX preparation; a steeper burst fall is not a valid discriminator alone. Ex vivo probe use only: no systemic, paediatric or dose statement. NP5A1 to NP5A3 (a measured GluN2B-sensitive share, a same-system comparison, assay context where it is missing)U21

Evolution: how it changes and when

The order is regenerated from a single command, with no new scheduler: without new information the result is identical byte for byte. Each version is a dated snapshot; when a group changes the reason is declared, and the entry of new compounds or the resolution of a tie are not mistaken for a change of judgement.

Classes of reason for a change of evaluation: new evidence, counter-evidence, identity correction, better pharmacological qualification, change of context, method revision. Changes that are not a change of judgement: new compound entry, resolution of a tie.

Which new developments prompt a re-evaluation

The new developments that prompt a re-evaluation of an intervention are detected by a fingerprint of its inputs; the fingerprint raises a flag, a reader decides. The existing daily radar flags the sources that changed.

New developmentHow it is detectedWhat is re-evaluated
T1_cards a card or packet of a ranked unit changes (assertion added, sign or depth corrected, abstention lifted, next step named)digest of the unit's cards, assertions, signs, scopes, depthspositions of the unit (coverage + view regenerate first), then group, class, reasons
T2_pertinence a pertinence row is added or changed (assertion judged pertinent to a need, sign, comparator, flags)digest of the unit's rows of coverage/assertion_pertinence.tsvthe F/C/P position of the card on that need and the specificity flags (G2a/G2b)
T3_receipts a new fulltext read receipt on a PMID that a ranked unit cites (a new reading of a source it rests on)count of receipts per cited PMID, read-only from the ledgera human re-reads the unit's cards against the new receipt; the digest only raises the flag, it never changes a group by itself
T4_needs a need observation, counter-evidence item, direction or work-order text changes for a need the unit is linked todigest of the linked needs' observation counts, direction and work-order change statementscontext of the unit (F3 needs a WWOX observation on the need; a direction change reverses what is consistent)

One-page summary

A first, explainable and updatable ordering of the interventions that LEGEND has identified so far. It expresses scientific promise and the priority of the next study. It is not a validated prediction of clinical benefit, not a probability of success, not a therapeutic recommendation and not medical advice.

The general selection and the two selections by aim on one A4 page. The full fields are in the cards above. Data as of: 2026-11-07; Version rules R4.

Evidence chains: from observation to experiment

Five chains taken from the most recent work cycles, read from left to right: observation in a WWOX system, need, mechanism, intervention, evidence, experiment. It is not a knowledge network and does not measure efficacy: it shows what each step rests on and what is missing.

Node labels are scientific text kept in the original language (English). A list of interactors (interactome) is never drawn as a causal edge. The figure scrolls horizontally within itself; the page does not. Chains written on 2026-10-29.

Legend. Edge type (line style and letter):
  • R experimental result: the cited experiment measured precisely that link
  • I inference: reasoning or transfer from another context, not measured
  • A association: co-occurrence, correlation or listing, without proof of modulation

Line under the node: scope of the datum: WWOX system; WWOX, other context; outside WWOX (another disease or protein); analysis on public data; proposed, not performed. UNRESOLVED: UNRESOLVED

Charts: an overview

Five charts only where they clarify. No chart measures efficacy: the number of biological pathways touched, of publications or of records enters no priority.

1. From the catalogue to the cards: what is counted, in which unit

How to read: each row has its own unit. The bars are to scale only within the same unit (records with records, families with families); cards are not a fraction of families.

  1. Catalogue records
    44.211 records
  2. Families (groupings of those records)
    40.268 families
  3. Families with a listed target
    2.002 families5,0% of the 40.268 families
  4. Families with a stated action on a target of a need
    622 families1,5% of the 40.268 families
  5. Candidate cards
    39 cards

    Different unit: compounds or interventions that have a written and read card.

Same quantity in records: 2.041 records with a listed target; 658 records with a stated action on a target of a need.

“Listed target” is a statement by a source about a target, not modulation and not recovery. “Stated action” says what the compound does on the target (inhibitor, agonist…): still a statement by a source, not evidence of an effect in WWOX. A family is not a distinct drug.

2. Access categories (predominantly US evidence)

Selection of compounds: from the catalogue to the next test

A funnel built from measured units, in this order: catalogued, usable with a calculation, actually evaluated, pertinent by mechanism, ready for a named test. Each indicator states its unit and its denominator; unknown or excluded compounds are counted with the reason. It is not a ranking and not a screen of the catalogue.

Units. A record is a source entry (a salt or a stereoisomer each count once, and are not distinct drugs). A family is the “compound” of this census and the number of families is an upper bound of the distinct compounds, because source-only entries are never merged by name. A card is an intervention or a class studied, not a compound.

Present in the catalogue does not mean evaluated

Hypotheses compared: research priority, model position and observed evidence

Nine hypotheses covering the two research aims and several types of intervention, chosen for coverage and not for merit. Three things remain separate, in distinct blocks: the research priority (position F, C or P and reason from the verification plan: it says where to take the next study, not whether the drug works), the model position and the evidence observed in a WWOX system. No combined score, no order.

Model position: what the comparison of methods says about this hypothesis (the predictive test, further below). Today it says nothing positive for any of the nine: “no position” means not evaluated, not rejected, and “no demonstrated advantage” concerns a method on the pilot subset, never a compound.

Key to the letters: F favourable hypothesis, C counter-evidence to be clarified, P missing premise; the number says where the support comes from (1 controlled in a WWOX system, 2 thin in WWOX, 3 from the target or from another disease). They are positions, not an order.

The scientific text of the blocks is in English, as in the original comparison. Concentrations and percentages cited from the sources describe external studies: they are not a guide to dosing and are not WWOX evidence. No calibrated clinical probability is shown, because none has been validated; the model percentile is not shown at all.

4-phenylbutyrate class and bile-acid chemical chaperones CMP-01

Research priority

4-phenylbutyrate class and bile-acid chemical chaperones A01_pba_class F3 on the need Rescuing a WWOX protein destabilised by a missense variant of the SDR domain
Verification plan: resolve a premise Rescuing a WWOX protein destabilised by a missense variant of the SDR domain

Model position

no model position for this hypothesis

  • Deliberately excluded from the comparison of methods because it has a curated card (so that the comparison could not be tuned to the compounds already discussed).
  • Outside the question of the comparison, which concerned a glycolysis/lactate transcript module: proteins, receptors and glia were not its subject.

Evidence observed in a WWOX system

None for the intervention in any WWOX system. The lesion side: one patient-fibroblast blot (one membrane, one exposure) shows transcript comparable to reference lines and no detectable protein band; fractions not separated.

Details: context, favourable, opposing and missing evidence, next experiment
Track and genotype
Track B: lesion-specific, a Q230P-class missense with residual protein; no meaning for null, nonsense or splice lesions
Depth of the benefit sought
deep: function per molecule of the rescued protein; a larger amount of protein is not function and is not read as rescue
Favourable: premise demonstrated
Other proteins: chemical chaperone or osmolyte raised a destabilised mutant with protein and function read together in some cases (GAT-1 variant; a soluble cytosolic client roughly doubled in soluble fraction). All are outside WWOX.
Opposing: opposite effects or counter-evidence
Wild-type protein rises too (not mutant-specific); partly trafficked variant not rescued by the class in one precedent; butyrate raised immature total protein with small function gain; toxicity ceiling near 4 mM in one paper; HDAC inhibition is quantitatively available at the applied levels and could be the operating mechanism, with transcriptional side effects.
Missing: premise not demonstrated
Where the Q230P-class protein is lost (never made, cleared, insoluble, epitope-invisible); any per-molecule WWOX function assay; whether the lesion is a stability lesion; which of three mechanism classes (chaperoning, HDAC6/HSP90 acetylation, class-I HDAC transcription) operates.
External precedents (they are not WWOX evidence)
Several cell, worm, fly, zebrafish and short mouse precedents in other proteins: cards record complete or partial full-text reads for the R1 papers; no WWOX test. Rationale was withdrawn once in this repository and narrowed, not refuted (IT5 P8).
Next experiment
Build the wild-type function ruler first: isogenic WWOX-null human neural line, wild-type WWOX titrated over at least five levels with a Tier 1 WW1-dependent readout and measured protein; then place the Q230P-class allele on the curve; only then a lever panel (class-I HDAC inhibitor; HDAC6-selective or pan-HDAC; HDAC-free chaperone and osmolytes) with mRNA flat and the null line unaffected as conditions. Outcomes fixed in advance in the card.
Experiment status
PROPOSED, not run; no measurement of this kind exists in the repository; its absence does not block the computational work

Proteasome-inhibitor class CMP-02

Research priority

Proteasome-inhibitor class A02_proteasome_inhibitor_class F3 on the need Rescuing a WWOX protein destabilised by a missense variant of the SDR domain
Verification plan: resolve a premise Rescuing a WWOX protein destabilised by a missense variant of the SDR domain

Model position

no model position for this hypothesis

  • Outside the question of the comparison, which concerned a glycolysis/lactate transcript module: proteins, receptors and glia were not its subject.

Evidence observed in a WWOX system

None for the intervention. No fractionation, half-life, inhibitor or synthesis datum exists for the exact variant.

Details: context, favourable, opposing and missing evidence, next experiment
Track and genotype
Track B: Q230P-class missense that is a proteasome substrate; a lysosomal route would make it ineffective; no meaning for null lesions
Depth of the benefit sought
deep only if stabilisation suffices; stabilisation without refolding is expected to raise inactive or insoluble protein for catalytic or folding lesions
Favourable: premise demonstrated
Cytosolic enzyme precedent (CBS): proteasome inhibition restored activity in vivo for a regulatory-domain allele and partly for catalytic-domain alleles; the route can be resolved per allele. Not WWOX.
Opposing: opposite effects or counter-evidence
Gain applies to wild type too (CBS wild-type half-life up about 7.7-fold); immune toxicity and toxic windows in controls; a heat-shock response confounds the readout; allele-selective failure (one allele not rescued in the mouse).
Missing: premise not demonstrated
That the Q230P-class protein is made and then cleared by the proteasome (the repository red-team record expects a lysosomal route); that recovered protein is functional; a safe exposure window.
External precedents (they are not WWOX evidence)
CBS and ASPA precedents read at the passages the card cites (IT6 P6, 17 statements checked): boost without repair, insoluble stabilised protein (ASPA), protein up with activity flat (CBS with HSP70 or HSF1 co-expression), toxic windows including in controls.
Next experiment
Route-first fate experiment on the exact variant in an expression-matched WWOX-null human system: soluble, pellet and total protein, mRNA in the same wells, pulse-chase half-life, proteasome, lysosome and ERAD arms side by side each on the ruler line and the null line with a viability readout. No protein with synthesis present closes this card for the allele.
Experiment status
PROPOSED, not run; no measurement of this kind exists in the repository; its absence does not block the computational work

AAV9-delivered human WWOX · AAV9-delivered human WWOX: endpoint families other than spike-wave discharges CMP-03

Research priority

AAV9-delivered human WWOX C01_aav9_wwox F2 on the need Restoring WWOX protein in neurons by adding the gene
AAV9-delivered human WWOX: endpoint families other than spike-wave discharges C04_aav9_endpoint_families F1 on the need Restoring WWOX protein in neurons by adding the gene C2 on the need Systemic metabolic decompensation
Verification plan: verificare un'ipotesi Restoring WWOX protein in neurons by adding the gene
Verification plan: chiarire una controevidenza Systemic metabolic decompensation

Model position

no model position for this hypothesis

  • It is not a compound with a target row: the network method does not apply.

Evidence observed in a WWOX system

Wwox-null mouse, vector given P0 to P5: spike-wave discharges not distinguishable from wild type at the high level (blinded, n 5); survival to 300 days at the high level comparable to the wild-type arm, the low level postpones death; weight equal at one age but survivor-conditioned; glucose unchanged; myelination dose relation never quantified; gliosis binary against wild type. Organoid AAV9-WWOX at week 10: hyperexcitability and transcript-level changes read at week 16 against non-treated organoids (not vector-treated).

Details: context, favourable, opposing and missing evidence, next experiment
Track and genotype
Track A: allele-blind in design (replaces the missing gene product); tested only in a null mouse; response in a missense or compound context with residual function is unmeasured
Depth of the benefit sought
deep: multi-endpoint restoration; shown for prevention in an early window, not for recovery after onset (one organoid endpoint aside)
Favourable: premise demonstrated
Prevention of the null phenotype by neuronal WWOX in the earliest postnatal window, in the strongest causal design of the corpus; neuron-restricted deletion reproduces the phenotype and neuron-restricted replacement reverses it.
Opposing: opposite effects or counter-evidence
Over-expression of a pro-apoptotic tumour suppressor with no ceiling measured and no surveillance; regionally uneven biodistribution; glucose endpoints null beside weight benefit (C2 on that need); wild-type arm itself lost about 29 percent by 300 days.
Missing: premise not demonstrated
Treatment after onset (mouse: unmeasured after P5); threshold versus steep continuum (two dose points); independent replication (two papers share a senior author); transfer to missense or compound alleles; tumour surveillance for an irreversibly delivered pro-apoptotic tumour suppressor; absolute vector quantity (uncertain by a factor of two in the source).
External precedents (they are not WWOX evidence)
The two mouse papers and the organoid paper are the only sources; the survival and motor comparators were re-read at the source in IT6 P2; the organoid single-cell data are deposited but not accessible. No other gene-addition precedent is used.
Next experiment
An intermediate-level arm (a fraction of the high level) carried to 300 days with survival, weight, glucose, ECoG and quantified myelin in the same animals, plus a pre-treatment baseline and treated-after-onset arms with a same-age untreated comparator. A failure moves the card to C2 by rule; a treated-after-onset arm decides whether the word recovery may be used.
Experiment status
PROPOSED, not run; no measurement of this kind exists in the repository; its absence does not block the computational work; needs a laboratory holding the vector, none known here

Evidence observed in a WWOX system

Details: context, favourable, opposing and missing evidence, next experiment
Track and genotype
Track A: allele-blind downstream metabolic lever; whether the axis is preserved in a catalytic-domain missense allele is an inference only
Depth of the benefit sought
partial: a metabolic consequence, not restoration of WWOX; no endpoint benefit is claimed
Favourable: premise demonstrated
LDHA transcript raised in two human neural transcript systems; HK and LDH activity raised in one human fibroblast line.
Opposing: opposite effects or counter-evidence
Stiripentol also inhibits mitochondrial complex I (isolated mouse heart and liver mitochondria, from tens of uM), so a metabolic effect is not an LDH effect and may recruit the integrated stress response; Ldh knockdown is detrimental in other fly amyloid models (authors' own citation); LDHB is the discordant gene in the P3 transfer test.
Missing: premise not demonstrated
LDH activity or lactate in WWOX-deficient human neural cells at matched maturity; that the elevation is not maturity or integrated-stress-response driven; that the candidate engages LDH in brain.
External precedents (they are not WWOX evidence)
Rico-Molina 2024 read in part (inhibition data), Bacq 2024 review opened at the pharmacokinetic passage; Sada 2015 not lawfully acquirable (abstract and secondary descriptions only). Nedosiran shows LDHA lowering tolerated in liver.
Next experiment
Lactate (isotope or enantiomer resolved) and LDH activity, LDHA and LDHB separately, in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells at matched maturity, with phospho-eIF2 alpha and ATF4 read beside LDH; the fly Ldh-alone arm; only then stiripentol against a selective LDHA tool at matched exposure. If lactate is not raised the need loses its WWOX observation and the card moves to P3 by rule.

PROPOSED, not run; no measurement of this kind exists in the repository; its absence does not block the computational work

Evidence observed in a WWOX system

PDK1 transcript up and HIF1alpha up in Wwox-null mouse embryonic fibroblasts; PDK transcript higher in a human knockout fibroblast line; PDK1 lower in sign only (inside the single-gene null) in two human neural transcript systems; PDH activity not different in the one human line; no PDH phosphorylation, flux or lactate measurement in any WWOX-deficient neural system. No compound given to any WWOX-deficient system.

Details: context, favourable, opposing and missing evidence, next experiment
Track and genotype
Track A: allele-blind in design; WWOX binds HIF1A through WW1, so the axis may be partly preserved in an SDR missense allele (inference)
Depth of the benefit sought
partial: a metabolic and possibly symptomatic effect; the card pursues no benefit endpoint and sharpens a decision
Favourable: premise demonstrated
The glycolytic end of the chain (LDHA, a HIF-type gene set) is raised in two human neural transcript systems; PDK-PDH restraint is documented after chemoconvulsant seizures in two non-WWOX epilepsy models.
Opposing: opposite effects or counter-evidence
Lowers glucose in adults and gluconeogenic precursors while hypoglycaemia is the Wwox-null phenotype (sign in a hypoglycaemic pup unmeasured); peripheral neuropathy is dose-limiting in adults; urinary oxalate +22 percent in a long-term cohort; rodent hepatotoxicity and neoplasia at high chronic doses; the general mechanism is self-inhibition of its own metabolism (GSTZ1), so exposure rises with repeated administration and varies with haplotype and age, whereas the one paediatric kinetic cohort (17 children) plateaued rather than accumulating - the two statements come from different sources and are not reconciled here; a slight pro-convulsant signal in one test.
Missing: premise not demonstrated
That PDH is restrained in a WWOX-deficient neural system and that the restraint is WWOX-dependent rather than seizure-secondary; the direction of the glucose response in a hypoglycaemic young animal.
External precedents (they are not WWOX evidence)
Paediatric congenital lactic acidosis randomized trial (lactate moved, no clinical outcome in six months), a long-term follow-up, a MELAS trial stopped early for neuropathy; the one seizure-endpoint test in a PDH-restrained model was negative (abstract level, closed); several of these at abstract or review level only.
Next experiment
In WWOX-deficient human neural cells against matched controls: PDHA1 Ser293 phosphorylation with total PDH, PDH activity and a glucose tracer into acetyl-CoA, citrate and lactate, then with a PDK inhibitor against vehicle reading the genotype-by-inhibitor interaction (free DCA exposure and a second inhibitor of different chemistry as controls).
Experiment status
PROPOSED, not run; no measurement of this kind exists in the repository; its absence does not block the computational work; cell access depends on a deposit that needs an access request that exists as a draft only and is not filed
